data.title: MCP Specification – version 2025-06-18 changes
data.author: owebmaster
data.article_summary:
《Model Context Protocol》最新规范（2025-06-18）摘要：

主要变更包括：
1. 移除对JSON-RPC批处理的支持（PR #416）。
2. 增加对结构化工具输出的支持（PR #371）。
3. 将MCP服务器分类为OAuth资源服务器，并添加受保护的资源元数据以发现授权服务器（PR #338）。
4. 要求MCP客户端实现RFC 8707中描述的资源指示器，以防止恶意服务器获取访问令牌（PR #734）。
5. 明确安全考虑和最佳实践，增加安全最佳实践页面。
6. 增加对引出的支持，使服务器能够在交互过程中请求额外信息（PR #382）。
7. 增加对工具调用结果中资源链接的支持（PR #603）。
8. 要求通过HTTP请求中的MCP-Protocol-Version头指定协商的协议版本（PR #548）。
9. 将生命周期操作中的“应”改为“必须”。

其他模式变更包括在接口类型中增加_meta字段，并在CompletionRequest中增加context字段等。完整变更日志可在GitHub查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（可能是某种通信协议或工具）的优缺点、应用场景、技术细节及安全问题

不同观点：
• **反对MCP复杂性**：
  - [neya] 认为MCP在编写后端软件时增加了不必要的复杂性，特别是每个API一个服务器的方式不合理，建议直接使用函数调用，避免管理过多的微服务。
  - [jjfoooo4] 强调MCP并没有节省显著的时间，特别是在本地开发时，开发者更希望对LLM调用的工具集有更严格的控制，而不是依赖MCP提供的中间件。

• **支持MCP的简化与改进**：
  - [dend] 赞赏MCP服务器授权的简化，感谢社区和Anthropic的贡献。
  - [gotts] 对MCP规范的快速改进表示赞赏，每次新版本发布都解决了一些集成中的问题。
  - [dgellow] 和 [swalsh] 则讨论了如何利用MCP简化任务自动化和认证管理，例如通过MCP OAuth代理和SSH服务器。

• **技术细节讨论**：
  - [eadmund] 提到MCP的批处理功能在某些情况下是有用的，尽管客户端可以自己处理批量响应。
  - [disintegrator] 认为WWW-Authenticate挑战的引入使得MCP服务器在处理OAuth流程时更加清晰。
  - [elliotbnvl] 对核心规范使用TypeScript而不是OpenAPI表示惊讶，但认为有一定道理。

• **MCP的应用场景与问题**：
  - [martinald] 分享了使用MCP处理数据集的经验，指出MCP在快速原型设计和非技术用户使用上的优势，但也提到认证和长时间任务处理上的困难。
  - [whazor] 建议增加资源更新/删除的审批流程，以便MCP服务器可以通过OAuth链接进行特定步骤的审批。

补充讨论：
• **安全问题**：
  - [fennecfoxy] 关注MCP服务器在恶意注入和数据泄露方面的安全性问题。
  
• **功能需求**：
  - [freed0mdox] 提出MCP缺少合理的异步回调机制，以便查询模型并返回操作结果。
  - [practal] 询问是否有流行的MCP主机支持采样功能。

争议焦点：
• **MCP的必要性与复杂性**：
  - 反对者认为MCP增加了不必要的复杂性，特别是在后端开发和本地开发环境中，而支持者则强调其在自动化、快速原型设计和特定任务简化上的优势。

the previous revision,
2025-03-26
.
​
Major changes
Remove support for JSON-RPC
batching
(PR
#416
)
Add support for
structured tool output
(PR
#371
)
Classify MCP servers as
OAuth Resource Servers
,
adding protected resource metadata to discover the corresponding Authorization server.
(PR
#338
)
Require MCP clients to implement Resource Indicators as described in
RFC 8707
to prevent
malicious servers from obtaining access tokens.
(PR
#734
)
Clarify
security considerations
and best practices
in the authorization spec and in a new
security best practices page
.
Add support for
elicitation
, enabling servers to request additional
information from users during interactions.
(PR
#382
)
Add support for
resource links
in
tool call results. (PR
#603
)
Require
negotiated protocol version to be specified
via
MCP-Protocol-Version
header in subsequent requests when using HTTP (PR
#548
).
Change
SHOULD
to
MUST
in
Lifecycle Operation
​
Other schema changes
Add
_meta
field to additional interface types (PR
#710
),
and specify
proper usage
.
Add
context
field to
CompletionRequest
, providing for completion requests to include
previously-resolved variables (PR
#598
).
Add
title
field for human-friendly display names, so that
name
can be used as a programmatic
identifier (PR
#663
)

data.title: Visual History of the Latin Alphabet
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章概述了从公元前200年到近代西方书法字体的演变历程。文章详细介绍了不同历史时期的代表性字体，如古代拉丁字母、罗马 monumental 字体、罗马草书、卡罗林小写体、哥特字体、人文主义小写体、文艺复兴时期的安提瓜字体、巴洛克和古典主义时期的草书及无衬线字体等。每个字体都与具体的历史文献或碑文相关联，展示了字体的发展和应用背景，如《特拉扬柱》上的 Capitalis Monumentalis 和《古滕堡圣经》中的 Textura 字体。文章还提到了各时期字体在书籍、碑文和手稿中的使用实例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英文拼写改革及字母演变的历史与可视化

不同观点：
• matada_ 认为英语拼写中存在冗余字母，去除这些字母可以使初学者更容易学习，并引用了关于英语拼写改革的维基百科页面作为参考。
• WillAdams 分享了F.W. Goudy的书中关于小写字母g从大写形式演变而来的内容，并提到在一个项目中使用不同年代的字体来体现层级关系，可以产生不错的效果。
• rf15 对可视化表示失望，认为它没有展示字体风格演变的关系和地域性，并且对现代字体发明被视为拉丁字母变体但未展示其变体的做法表示不满。
• behnamoh 质疑为何使用如"sh"和"ch"的字母组合而不是创造新字符，并提到其他语言可能有不同的处理方式。
• aitchnyu 原本期待能看到楔形文字和腓尼基字母等每个字母的祖先，并提到1990年代的世界图书百科全书展示了各个文明的字母演变。

补充讨论：
• bryanrasmussen 询问了用于创建可视化的图书馆和工具。
• tempodox 对Rustic Capitals中相似字母的不同形式是否暗示不同发音或有其他功能表示好奇。
• naikrovek 认为可视化更像是几种字体的演变，而不是拉丁字母的演变。
• paganel 赞赏可视化，并分享了关于中世纪意大利文书学中不同书写风格（如La minuscola cancelleresca）的知识，提供了一个意大利语的链接。
• hemmert 简单表达了对可视化的赞赏。

争议焦点：
- 可视化的有效性和全面性是讨论的争议点。rf15和naikrovek都对可视化的呈现方式和内容深度表示不满，认为它没有充分展示字母和字体风格的演变关系及地域性。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为CashflowD (CFD) 的加密货币分析引擎，由Caudena公司开发，旨在解决区块链数据快速增长带来的分析挑战。传统分析工具因速度慢、成本高且基于过时的数据库技术，难以应对海量数据。CFD通过现代C++构建，采用内存数据库和即时编译查询引擎，实现基础设施成本降低200至400倍。它提供实时分析，部分查询在亚毫秒级返回，支持可验证且法庭可接受的路径，进行复杂的地址聚类和风险评估。其架构通过高度优化的自定义存储和激进的数据打包技术，处理大规模数据，特别适用于如Solana等已超过400TB的区块链。文章强调CFD在性能和经济性上的突破，为金融机构和调查机构提供了前所未有的分析能力。

主要讨论点：围绕Prism项目的技术实现、优化细节、语言选择、应用场景及其开源可能性的讨论。

不同观点：
• **关于C++优化的兴趣**：[canyp]对C++优化带来的成本大幅降低表示赞赏，并询问了具体的优化技巧和细节。

• **关于可移植性与无锁实现的讨论**：[plq]关注无锁数据结构的可移植性，询问在不同处理器上的行为差异以及如何测试无锁实现的正确性。他还提到了使用现有库（如folly的RCU实现）的可能性。

• **与JVM实现的比较**：[Snoozus]提到他们在2016年使用JVM实现了类似系统，并询问Prism是否能够动态撤销集群，以及是否为每个客户单独运行实例以隔离信息访问。

• **语言选择的理由**：[generalenvelope]对选择C++而非Rust表示好奇，并询问了C++相对于Rust等内存安全语言的优势和现有生态系统的不足之处。

• **与其他数据库的性能对比**：[CharlesW]质疑从零开始构建自定义内存数据库的资源投入，并询问Prism与Memgraph、KX kdb+、Apache Ignite、TigerGraph等数据库的性能对比。

• **术语澄清**：[layer8]对“barebone servers”这一术语提出疑问，认为可能是“bare-metal servers”。

补充讨论：
• **关于信息隔离的应用场景**：[Snoozus]提到执法机构（如FBI）告知某些钱包属于同一参与者时，如何在系统中实现该信息的可视化，而不泄露给其他机构（如Europol）。

• **对区块链服务的兴趣**：[BiraIgnacio]表示对“区块链服务”领域公司存在的好奇，并对C++工作表示赞赏。

• **开源可能性**：[gnhe2009]询问Prism是否会开源。

• **对项目性质的质疑**：[intelVISA]认为该项目像是“griftware”（可能指以创新为名的敛财工具）。

• **关于Monero的匿名性讨论**：[folk111]询问XMR/Monero是否真的不可追踪。

• **对隐私和监控的关注**：[kayamon]质疑项目是否涉及对用户的监控。

• **AMA中的其他问题**：[wslh]感谢AMA活动，并提出几个问题，包括是否可能开源数据库、支持的区块链类型以及是否存在测试Prism的“HN Code”。

争议焦点：
• **选择C++而非Rust的合理性**：部分讨论围绕为何选择C++而非Rust展开，涉及对内存安全语言与现有生态系统的讨论。

• **自定义数据库的必要性**：有观点质疑从零开始构建自定义数据库的必要性，认为可能存在现成解决方案。

• **项目性质与隐私问题**：部分评论对项目的真实目的和隐私问题表示关注，甚至提出质疑。

Real-Time, Court-Admissible Crypto Intelligence at 1/400th the Cost of Inferior Legacy Systems
The explosion of blockchain data isn’t just a challenge; it’s a crisis for conventional analytics. Financial institutions, investigators, and law enforcement agencies are hamstrung by tools that are too slow, expensive, and built on legacy database technologies incapable of keeping pace. Critical insights are missed, opportunities vanish, and illicit activities remain obscured by systems that offer only a shallow view of the complex reality.
At Caudena, we didn’t just tweak an existing solution; we architected
CashflowD (CFD)
from the ground up, a proprietary in-memory database and JIT-compiling query engine built in modern C++. The result is
a 200X to 400X reduction in infrastructure costs
. Our competitors’ capabilities are
significantly inferior
and cannot produce the same depth of analysis. We deliver true real-time analytics, with some queries returning in
sub-millisecond timeframes – often bottlenecked only by network latency
. This isn’t an incremental improvement; it’s a paradigm shift that unlocks previously impossible analytical capabilities, provides court-admissible evidence, and fundamentally changes the economics of blockchain intelligence, allowing us to empower organizations to outmaneuver and outperform all existing solutions.
CFD is a cryptocurrency analytics engine meticulously designed to process blockchain data at scale, perform sophisticated address clustering with
verifiable, court-admissible paths,
conduct in-depth investigations, and assign robust, interpretable risk scores. This solution is engineered for those who demand complex analysis of the blockchain, involving massive operations on its ever-expanding data — from financial institutions and compliance teams to investigators facing down sophisticated adversaries. The architecture of CFD doesn’t just handle vast data volumes; it crushes them, especially critical as blockchains like Solana already exceed
400TB and are projected to reach 1 Petabyte within a year
, rendering less efficient systems economically unviable.
Under the Hood: The Architecture of Unrivaled Speed, Power, and Efficiency
The “magic” behind CFD isn’t magic at all; it’s the result of deep C++ expertise, a first-principles approach to data management, and an obsession with performance that leaves competitors in the dust.
1. The In-Memory C++ Core: Where Every Nanosecond Counts
Conventional tools hit a wall with I/O and struggle with data volume. We demolished that wall and built a highway.
The entirety of the relevant blockchain data processed by CFD resides in RAM, processed by our custom C++ engine. This eliminates I/O bottlenecks entirely, forming the bedrock of our sub-second query capabilities. However, “in-memory” alone isn’t enough; it’s how we manage that memory that sets us apart, especially when dealing with Petabyte-scale projections.
Highly Optimized Custom Storage:
We don’t rely on off-the-shelf databases. CFD utilizes an in-memory storage system, intelligently mapping less-frequently accessed data to disk when necessary, ensuring RAM is prioritized for active computation. This allows transaction processing and the time to incorporate new blocks and addresses to be extraordinarily fast.
Aggressive Data Packing & Representation:
Every bit per transaction is worth saving when dealing with billions of transactions and terabytes of data. Our data is packed to reduce size – sometimes aligned for CPU cache efficiency, sometimes stored in variable-length structures. We employ small-vector optimizations where sensible and even advanced techniques like pointer tagging. Standard Linux pointers are 48 bits, leaving 16 (or even 17 user-space) upper bits free. We leverage this, for instance, by reserving bits to treat a value in a special way – if a specific bit is set, the value might be interpreted as a pointer to a larger 128-bit value, or an index into a specialized dictionary, avoiding the need to use (say) 16 bits for values when 8 bits cover 99.99% of cases. This attention to data representation is how we manage to hold and process colossal datasets entirely in-memory.
Consider this illustrative C++ snippet, showcasing our philosophy of deriving properties from an object’s memory alignment to wring every ounce of performance from the hardware:
struct OddEven { /* ... members ... */ bool is_even() const; };
bool OddEven::is_even() const {
return (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this) / sizeof(OddEven)) % 2 == 0;
}
// Or for block-aligned items:
size_t Item::get_index() const {
return reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this) % block_alignment / sizeof(Item);
}
Securing such block alignment can be achieved by acquiring
block_alignment * 2
memory (e.g., via
mmap
with
PROT_NONE
) and then unmapping extra pages. This meticulous, low-level engineering is pervasive throughout CFD.

data.title: Curved-Crease Sculpture
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: Erik Demaine和Martin Demaine探索了沿曲线折痕折叠纸张时形成的自然平衡形态。这种自折叠折纸的形态及其潜在应用，包括可展开结构、制造和自组装，尚不完全理解。他们的作品将平面纸张转变为旋转的立体雕塑，赋予作品生命感。自2008年起，他们创作了多个系列作品，如"Beethoven Series" (2021)、"Braille Series" (2023)等，并在多个博物馆和艺术馆展出。曲线折纸雕塑的历史可追溯至1920年代的包豪斯，具有悠久的历史。

主要讨论点：折纸与数学、艺术、科技的交集

不同观点：
• [hokumguru] 提到折纸与数学的结合，特别推荐了Eric Demaine和Robert Lang，并对比了已故艺术家Eric Joisel的艺术折纸作品，强调Joisel的作品在艺术上的独特性。
• [frakt0x90] 关注Eric Demaine的教学能力，尤其是通过其讲座学习动态编程，指出了Demaine在教育方面的贡献。
• [FuriouslyAdrift] 引入了Le Klint的折纸灯罩，强调了实用性与美学的结合，并提供了相关工作坊的信息。
• [srean] 讨论了折纸中的直线折叠与几何学的关系，指出折纸在提供直线方面的实用性。
• [TheCoreh] 将折纸艺术与椭圆曲线艺术联系起来，提出了关于灵感来源的疑问。
• [boulos] 推荐了纪录片《Between the Folds》，认为该片对折纸爱好者非常有价值。
• [esafak] 认为折纸与数学结合的工作可能是学术界中最有趣的工作之一。
• [talkingtab] 提出了折纸技术在其他领域的应用，例如通过曲线折叠形成特定形状的容器。
• [bdbenton5255] 强调了折纸作为现代与古典艺术交汇点的魅力，关注其复杂性与细节。
• [davidpfarrell] 表达了对Curved-Crease Sculptures的惊讶与欣赏。
• [kazinator] 指出曲线折叠雕塑的历史可以追溯到1920年代的包豪斯，认为这一历史相对较新。
• [wiz21c] 幽默地提出让尚未成熟的AGI机器人尝试折纸，以观察其进展。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多位在折纸与数学、艺术领域有影响力的人物及其作品，如Eric Demaine、Robert Lang和Eric Joisel。
• 讨论涉及折纸技术的实际应用，如灯罩制作和容器成型。
• 提到了教育资源和纪录片，如《Between the Folds》，为对折纸感兴趣的人提供了进一步学习的途径。
• 争议的焦点可能在于折纸艺术的起源与发展时间，部分评论对这一历史的“新近性”表示惊讶。

Curved-Crease Sculpture
by
Erik Demaine
and
Martin Demaine
When folded along curved creases,
paper shapes itself into a natural equilibrium form.
These equilibria are poorly understood, especially for curved creases.
We are exploring what shapes are possible in this genre of self-folding
origami, with applications to deployable structures, manufacturing, and
self-assembly.  This transformation of flat paper into swirling surfaces
creates sculpture that feels alive.

data.title: Finding Dead Websites
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Marginalia Search引擎实现的一个新功能，用于检测网站的可用性和重大变更，以避免提供死链接并提高数据质量。该系统通过HEAD请求和DNS查询检测网站是否在线，并通过分析DNS历史、证书信息、网站安全状态及其他头部信息（如X-Powered-By和Server）来识别网站所有权变更或重大改版。

系统将数据分为两类表格：一类存储当前快照，另一类存储历史事件数据。可用性信息和网站指纹分别存储在不同表格中，以优化性能。DNS信息则单独存储在第三张表中。

为应对事件数据增长过快的问题，系统采用按月分区的策略，将旧数据导出并压缩存储，以避免表格过大影响性能。通过这些措施，Marginalia Search能够有效维护数据质量并优化爬虫行为。

Finding Dead Websites
Posted: 2025-06-17
As some of the work planned for Marginalia Search this year has been progressing a bit faster than anticipated, there was time to implement an unplanned change.
This post details the implementation of a system for detecting when servers are online, to avoid serving dead links and improve data quality, and for detecting when websites have significant changes including ownership transfers and parking.
Table Of Contents
Feature Rationale
Data Representation
Live Data
Event Data
Change Detection Details
Availability Detection
Ownership Changes
DNS
Implementation Hurdles
Scheduling
Certificate Validation
Conclusions
Feature Rationale
Availability detection is useful not just for filtering out dead links in the search results, but for informing the crawler that it should stop trying to reach a dead domain, as well as a host of other things. Likewise, ownership change detection is relevant to the crawler, which might be informed to do a clean recrawl instead of an incremental one, and could also enter as a factor in domain ranking.
Since misbehaving bots spamming web servers with unwanted requests is a very big and hot issue, and reputation is incredibly important for a small search engine like Marginalia, the feature is implemented with the design constraint to as best possible only do this with only HEAD requests, normally sent 1-2 times per day per domain; and also DNS queries on a similar interval.
So how much information can you really get from a HEAD request and a DNS query? It’s possible to extract a fairly large number of factors, many of which
weakly
indicate an ownership change, but when taken together paint a fairly lucid picture.
The ownership change detection looks at DNS history, details of the certificate, the security posture of the website, other headers like
X-Powered-By
and
Server
. One or a few of these changing is normal, but many of them changing at the same time indicates at the very least a major redesign or infrastructure overhaul.
As just about the only thing we do not use to detect changes and uptime is ICMP ping, the name
ping-process
was chosen for the process that is responsible for availability and change monitoring.
Data Representation
The data is split into two categories of tables, one holding the latest snapshot, and one holding historical events.
Simplified sketch of the database model
Live Data
One of the first design decision was splitting the table holding current availability information into two.
One table holds basic availability information, such as whether the website is available, error classification, when it was last seen, and so forth.
The other table holds a fingerprint of the website, its certificate, security posture, other headers. This is a fairly exhaustive fingerprint because it’s hard to know beforehand which information will be useful. The data is still small enough for this to be affordable.
The argument for this split is that the security information is a very wide column that won’t be populated for any server we can’t reach, where we can’t find a certificate and we get headers.
Having a separate column for the security fingerprint also means we don’t lose access to the last viable fingerprint if a server becomes temporarily unavailable.
In many cases we only want to know if the server is up or not; so reading a ton of irrelevant data isn’t going to do the performance any favors. We’re only generally interested in full security information when running analytics jobs to identify ownership changes and looking for other patterns, and this will never be done in real time.
DNS information is in a third table because it operates on a different set of domains than http(s)-traffic. While there is overlap between the set of domains that make sense to try to connect to, and the ones that make sense to
dig
, there are also domains that are in only one of the two sets.
Event Data
Change information is stored in separate events tables. These are treated as effectively immutable, append-only. This is to cope with the performance implications of the events tables (eventually) growing significantly larger than the live snapshot tables.
The events tables store a summary of the changes, as well as persisting the full before-and-after state of the information tables as compressed JSON. This trade-off allows the retention of full historical snapshots, with smaller on-disk storage, while making schema changes somewhat more tolerable as the events tables are likely to grow very large over time.
To avoid having these tables grow forever, they’re partitioned by month. This makes it possible to run a job which exports old data into e.g. parquet or a columnar storage, and then truncating the partitions as-needed. Unlike DELETE-based flows, this can safely be done while the system is running without long table locks as new data is predictably always inserted into a different partition.

data.title: Show HN: A DOS-like hobby OS written in Rust and x86 assembly
data.author: krustowski
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了**rou2exOS Rusted Edition**，这是一个用Rust重写的类似DOS的操作系统，是RoureXOS的第二版。项目文件包括内核、启动加载器、构建脚本等，用户可以通过QEMU模拟器运行附带的ISO镜像，或在x86_64硬件上通过USB启动。构建步骤包括安装Rust及相关工具、编译内核和启动加载器、生成ISO镜像，并提供了测试ICMP/SLIP网络功能的方法。该项目主要使用Rust编写，包含少量汇编代码，适用于操作系统开发学习。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个类似于DOS的业余项目，具有网络栈、多架构支持等特性，引发的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• [rollcat] 认为该项目是一个内存安全的语言编写的、支持x86_64架构，并计划支持Arm架构，具有网络栈，可以从CD启动或通过multiboot启动，比DOS更具技术优势。
• [Toritori12] 赞扬了项目，并认为这是一个错过引用Linux早期名言的时机，即"只是一个业余项目，不会像Linux那样庞大且专业"。
• [mct] 对项目中使用SLIP和slattach(1)表示赞赏，并询问其他人是否在macOS上使用过SLIP来实现跨平台的网络栈接口，认为SLIP比tun/tap或utun更简单。
• [OhNotAPaper] 对选择x86架构表示好奇，质疑是否因为资源丰富、指令格式特殊或启动顺序复杂，并询问如何在多架构上支持类似DOS的操作系统，考虑到DOS本身与程序、系统代码和架构紧密相关。
• [pndy] 询问是否计划添加对捷克语 diacritics 的支持。
• [ta12653421] 以幽默的方式询问该项目是否能运行Crysis游戏。
• [mixmastamyk] 表示希望有类似DOS的环境来替代当前的UEFI环境和shell，并询问项目是否支持FAT12以外的分区格式如GPT，以及输出方式是否类似于DOS的视频硬件操作。

补充讨论：
• [DrNosferatu] 质疑该项目是否类似于DOS但并不兼容DOS。
• [90s_dev] 询问项目是否使用了自定义的VGA驱动，并且是否是用Rust编写的。
• [m00dy] 认为项目需要一个事件队列来支持异步运行时。
• [jmmv] 不理解该项目为何被称为"DOS-like"，因为命令名称与DOS并不匹配，且架构和功能集完全不同。

争议焦点：
• 项目是否真的可以被称为"DOS-like"，特别是从[jmmv]和[DrNosferatu]的评论来看，他们质疑项目与DOS的实际相似性。
• 对于选择x86架构的原因存在疑问，[OhNotAPaper]对多架构支持如何实现表示关注。

这些讨论反映了社区对该项目技术实现细节的关注，以及对项目命名和定位的不同看法。

rou2exOS Rusted Edition
A second iteration of the RoureXOS operating system, rewritten in Rust.
Original RoureXOS (a blog post)
rou2exOS Rusted Edition (a blog post)
To run the OS, you can use the attached ISO image from any Release, and run it in QEMU emulator. The system was also tested on x86_64 baremetal (booted from the USB flash disk).
How to build and run
#
install Rust and its dependencies
make init
#
make sure you have `xorriso`, `net-tools` and `grub2-tools` installed (Linux)
dnf install xorriso net-tools grub2-tools qemu qemu-common qemu-system-x86
#
compile the kernel and stage2 bootloader, link it into an ELF binary and bake into an ISO image with GRUB stage1 bootloader
make build
#
run the QEMU emulation with ISO image (respectively with additional floppy image attached as well)
make run_iso
make run_iso_floppy
#
(alternative) run the kernel exclusively only (needs the `bootloader` dependency in Cargo.toml to be added)
cargo bootimage
make run
How to test ICMP/SLIP
Run the kernel in QEMU to get the
pty
number in stdout:
make run
char device redirected to /dev/pts/3 (label serial0)
Listen for SLIP packets and create a
sl0
interface:
sudo slattach -L -p slip -s 115200 /dev/pts/3
sudo ifconfig sl0 192.168.3.1 pointopoint 192.168.3.2 up
Catch packets using
tcpdump
:
sudo tcpdump -i sl0

data.title: DNA floating in the air tracks wildlife, viruses, even drugs
data.author: karlperera
data.article_summary: 一篇2025年6月3日的文章报道，佛罗里达大学的研究表明，通过空气中的环境DNA（eDNA）可以追踪从野生动物到非法药物等多种信息。研究人员使用简单的空气过滤器捕捉空气中的DNA，能够识别出包括美洲虎、蜘蛛等动物的踪迹，甚至检测到如大麻、鸦片等毒品的存在。此外，该技术还能监测人类病原体和过敏原，帮助追踪新兴疾病。研究显示，这种方法高效且经济，单个研究人员一天内即可完成分析，但同时也引发了对敏感遗传数据伦理问题的关注。这项技术为生态研究和物种保护开辟了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从空气中获取DNA技术的发展及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [arjie] 认为将自己的DNA序列公开存储存在风险，并将自己视为因公开DNA而可能遭遇危险的警示例子。该评论关注个人DNA公开可能带来的安全隐患。

• [robwwilliams] 指出在处理人类或低模板DNA时，需高度谨慎以避免空气中的DNA污染。评论强调了实验操作中的技术细节，如PCR扩增的循环数，关注实验技术的精确性。

• [Noelia-] 认为从空气中获取DNA技术的进步令人印象深刻，但同时也带来了一些令人担忧的隐私和伦理问题。她强调需要讨论技术的边界，以确保人类拥有私密空间。

• [altacc] 对技术进步表示惊叹，从过去需要13年时间的人类基因组测序到现在可以快速从空气中获取DNA。该评论主要表达对技术快速发展的感慨。

• [karlperera] 提出了关于隐私问题的担忧，特别是在公共或私人空间中收集和测序人类漂浮DNA的潜在影响，提出了“我们能否做”和“我们是否应该做”的伦理问题。

Science News
from research organizations
DNA floating in the air tracks wildlife, viruses -- even drugs
Date:
June 3, 2025
Source:
University of Florida
Summary:
Environmental DNA from the air, captured with simple air filters, can track everything from illegal drugs to the wildlife it was originally designed to study.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
Dublin is known as a city where you can enjoy a few pints of Guiness, get a warm welcome from the locals and hear lively traditional music drifting out of pubs and into the city air.
But it's not just music floating on the breeze. The air of Dublin also contains cannabis, poppy, even magic mushrooms -- at least their DNA.
That's according to a new study that reveals the power of DNA, vacuumed up from the air, which can track everything from elusive bobcats to illicit drugs.
"The level of information that's available in environmental DNA is such that we're only starting to consider what the potential applications can be, from humans, to wildlife to other species that have implications for human health," said David Duffy, Ph.D., a professor of wildlife disease genomics at the University of Florida and lead author of a new study showing the widespread utility of DNA vacuumed from the air.
Housed at UF's Whitney Laboratory for Marine Bioscience, Duffy's lab developed new methods for deciphering environmental DNA, also known as eDNA, to study sea turtle genetics. They've expanded the tools to study every species -- including humans -- from DNA captured in environmental samples like water, soil and sand.
But these errant strands of DNA do not just settle into muddy soil or flow along rivers. The air itself is infused with genetic material. A simple air filter running for hours, days or weeks can pick up signs of nearly every species that grows or wanders nearby.
"When we started, it seemed like it would be hard to get intact large fragments of DNA from the air. But that's not the case. We're actually finding a lot of informative DNA," Duffy said. "That means you can study species without directly having to disturb them, without ever having to see them. It opens up huge possibilities to study all the species in an area simultaneously, from microbes and viruses all the way up to vertebrates like bobcats and humans, and everything in between."
As a proof of concept, the researchers showed that they could pick up signs of hundreds of different human pathogens from the Dublin air, including viruses and bacteria. Such surveillance could help scientists track emerging diseases. The same method can track common allergens, like peanut or pollen, more precisely than is currently possible, the scientists discovered.
In another test of the power of eDNA, Duffy's lab was also able to identify the origin of bobcats and spiders whose DNA was hoovered up from air in a Florida forest. With little more than an air filter, scientists could track endangered species and identify where they came from, all without having to lay eyes on skittish animals or root around forest floors for scat samples. When trying to save and conserve wildlife, knowing where an animal originates from can be as important as knowing where it currently is.
This powerful analysis was paired with impressive speed and efficiency. The team demonstrated that a single researcher could process DNA for every species in as little as a day using compact, affordable equipment, and software hosted in the cloud. That quick turnaround is orders of magnitude faster than would have been possible just a few years ago and opens up advanced environmental studies to more scientists around the world. The same tools can potentially identify sensitive human genetic data, which is why Duffy and his collaborators have called for ethical guardrails for the rapidly developing field of eDNA.
"It seems like science fiction, but it's becoming science fact," Duffy said. "The technology is finally matching the scale of environmental problems."

主要讨论点：庆祝Juneteenth（六月节）及其意义，以及对该节日名称的讨论。

不同观点：
• macrael的观点：庆祝Juneteenth，并表达希望国家能够改变，未来不再通过战争来解放人民。强调节日的历史意义和和平愿景。

• moomoo11的观点：支持庆祝Juneteenth，认为美国自1776年以来一直在推动社会进步，尽管个人行为多出于私利，但整体社会在不断向前发展。相较于独裁、腐败或宗教 intolerance 的国家，美国社会更为优越。

• juddlyon的观点：赞赏关于Juneteenth的照片和故事，认为争论节日名称是舍本逐末。强调应关注节日的内涵和重要性，而不是纠结于名称。

• sfblah的观点：更喜欢使用“Emancipation Day”这一名称，认为“Juneteenth”不是一个真正的词，容易让人困惑，主张使用更直白的表述。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点集中在对“Juneteenth”这一名称的理解和接受程度上。部分人认为该名称不够直观，而另一部分人则认为纠结名称会忽略节日的真正意义。
• moomoo11的评论还涉及对美国历史和政治制度的评价，认为尽管有缺陷，美国社会整体上在不断进步。
• juddlyon特别强调了对节日背后故事和意义的关注，认为名称争论偏离了节日的核心价值。

data.title: Why do we need DNSSEC?
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了为什么我们需要DNSSEC。DNS最初设计时并未 prioritize 安全性，其主要功能是将人类易读的域名转换为设备所需的IP地址。由于DNS解析器无法验证权威服务器响应的真实性，可能存在数据被篡改的风险。DNSSEC（DNS安全扩展）通过为DNS提供认证功能来解决这一问题，确保响应未被 tamper 过，但它不像HTTPS那样加密数据。DNSSEC只验证数据完整性，不提供数据保密性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DNSSEC的实用性、重要性及其替代方案

不同观点：
• **对DNSSEC的实用性持怀疑态度**：[tptacek] 认为DNSSEC并没有那么重要，因为经过25年的推广仍未广泛应用，且该协议的名称听起来比实际作用更大。他同时对DNS提供商制作卡通解释器表示不解。
• **技术实现细节和要求**：[Bender] 指出当前DNSSEC的技术实现过于复杂，需要更好的自动化和集成，例如自动签名、加密区域传输等功能。他还提到希望看到根服务器支持DoT（DNS over TLS），并希望看到更多的安全性检查。
• **迭代查询的替代方案**：[1vuio0pswjnm7] 提出使用迭代查询作为递归查询的替代方案，认为这可能比DNSSEC更有效。他提供了自己实现迭代查询的例子，并指出目前权威服务器不加密响应的问题。
• **政府和商业阻碍**：[anonymousiam] 提到Dan Kaminsky揭示了DNSSEC的重要性，特别是在防止中间人攻击和流量欺骗方面。然而，一些政府和商业实体（如Network Solutions）不积极支持DNSSEC，甚至通过额外收费来限制其使用。
• **对PKI体系的不信任**：[Avamander] 认为DNSSEC只是另一种PKI体系，且无法摆脱不良运营者的影响，因此不值得依赖。
• **可选标准和可见性问题**：[burnt-resistor] 指出可选的替代标准因为缺乏可见性而很少被使用，并提到过去有一些不友好的DNSSEC浏览器扩展被取消。
• **对国家行为体的无效性**：[coretx] 认为DNSSEC对国家行为体无效，无法提供保护。
• **用户体验和意识问题**：[Zaylan] 提到普通用户无法感知哪些网站使用了DNSSEC，因为浏览器不会提示缺少DNSSEC，这使得用户难以关心这一问题。
• **易用性**：[UltraSane] 认为在AWS Route53上设置DNSSEC非常简单，并指出其在签名txt记录方面的实用性。
• **证书验证功能**：[aspbee555] 提到DNSSEC允许在DNS记录中包含证书颁发机构信息，从而验证证书的可信性。
• **区块链替代方案**：[jongjong] 提出可以使用区块链技术替代传统的DNS系统，构建去中心化的DNS系统，并提到已有项目（如Ethereum的.ETH域名和Unstoppable Domains）实现了类似功能。

补充讨论：
• **技术社区的态度**：[tialaramex] 提到对DNSSEC的质疑类似于C++社区对安全性的态度变化，暗示了对DNSSEC的批评和忽视可能逐渐转变。

争议焦点：
• DNSSEC的重要性：一方认为DNSSEC并未广泛应用且不那么重要，另一方则认为其在防止网络攻击方面至关重要。
• 技术实现的复杂性：有人指出当前的DNSSEC实现过于复杂，需要更多自动化和加密功能，而另一些人则认为已有易用的实现方案。
• 替代方案的可行性：部分人支持迭代查询或区块链技术作为DNSSEC的替代方案，认为这些技术可能更有效或更去中心化。

44320497.article_content:
Episode 1
Why do we need DNSSEC?
Good question! Why do we need DNSSEC?
DNS was created the Internet was tiny small.
Security was not a primary concern in its design.
Simply put, DNS main job is to translate human-friendly names to IP addresses needed by your laptop, phones, and other network devices.
DNS is like a big phone book that your devices use to fetch you a website, or deliver your emails.
DNS resolvers
are the ones in charge of tracking down this information for you.
And that data is often provided by
authoritative servers
.
But DNS resolvers have no way to verify the authenticity of a response from an authoritative server.
What if the response has been tampered with?
This is where
DNSSEC
comes in.
Resolvers? Authoritative name servers? What are all these things? Check out
HowDNS.works
for a refresher and come back here.
I’ll be waiting.
DNSSEC is short for Domain Name System Security Extensions.
Like HTTPS, DNSSEC provides a layer of security by allowing authenticated answers on top of DNS.
However, there is a important difference.
HTTPS encrypts traffic so no crabs can spy on your data.
DNSSEC signs DNS data
to detect that no crabs have been messing with your DNS responses.
Bad crab. Bad.
DNSSEC doesn't include full encryption like HTTPS does.
The data is not kept confidential and secret between the resolver and the authoritative server.
Let’s dig a bit deeper into DNSSEC. Ready?
Continue reading →

EnrichMCP
The ORM for AI Agents - Turn your data model into a semantic MCP layer
EnrichMCP is a Python framework that helps AI agents understand and navigate your data. Built on MCP (Model Context Protocol), it adds a semantic layer that turns your data model into typed, discoverable tools - like an ORM for AI.
What is EnrichMCP?
Think of it as SQLAlchemy for AI agents. EnrichMCP automatically:
Generates typed tools
from your data models
Handles relationships
between entities (users → orders → products)
Provides schema discovery

Validates all inputs/outputs
with Pydantic models
Works with any backend

data.title: Star Quakes and Monster Shock Waves
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: Caltech研究人员利用超级计算机模拟了黑洞吞噬中子星的过程。当一个中子星与黑洞接近时，黑洞的引力会导致中子星表面发生“星震”，其表壳会像地震一样破裂。模拟展示了中子星在被吞噬前约一秒内发生的剧烈变化，并预测了天文学家可能观测到的光耀。在另一项研究中，模拟还展示了中子星破裂后产生的强大冲击波，以及随后形成的罕见天体——“黑洞脉冲星”。这种天体是黑洞在吞噬中子星后，短时间内通过磁风模拟脉冲星特征形成的。这些模拟首次详细展示了此类天体事件的物理过程。

Star Quakes and Monster Shock Waves
Star Quakes and Monster Shock Waves
June 03, 2025
Caltech researchers simulate a black hole consuming a neutron star
Across the cosmos, many stars can be found in pairs, gracefully circling one another. Yet one of the most dramatic pairings occurs between two orbiting black holes, formed after their massive progenitor stars exploded in supernova blasts. If these black holes lie close enough together, they will ultimately collide and form an even more massive black hole. Sometimes a black hole is orbited by a neutron star—the dense corpse of a star also formed from a supernova explosion but which contains less mass than a black hole. When these two bodies finally merge, the black hole will typically swallow the neutron star whole.
To better understand the extreme physics underlying such a grisly demise, researchers at Caltech are using supercomputers to simulate black hole–neutron star collisions. In one
study appearing in
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
, the team, led by
Elias Most
, a Caltech assistant professor of theoretical astrophysics, developed the most detailed simulation yet of the violent quakes that rupture a neutron star's surface roughly a second before the black hole consumes it.
"The neutron star's crust will crack open just like the ground in an earthquake," Most says. "The black hole's gravity first shears the surface, causing quakes in the star and the opening of rifts."
While cracks in the crust of a neutron star had been predicted before, the simulation is the first to demonstrate what kinds of light flares astronomers might see in the future when pointing telescopes in space and on the ground at such an event.
"This goes beyond educated models for the phenomenon—it is an actual simulation that includes all the relevant physics taking place when the neutron star breaks like an egg," says co-author
Katerina Chatziioannou
, assistant professor of physics at Caltech and a William H. Hurt Scholar.
Zoom In to Image
These three panels are taken from a supercomputer simulation of a merger between a black hole (large black circle) and a neutron star (colored blob). The images, which move forward in time from left to right, show how the intense gravity of the black hole stretches the neutron star, before the black hole ultimately consumes it.
Credit: Elias Most/Caltech
Image Lightbox
These three panels are taken from a supercomputer simulation of a merger between a black hole (large black circle) and a neutron star (colored blob). The images, which move forward in time from left to right, show how the intense gravity of the black hole stretches the neutron star, before the black hole ultimately consumes it.
Credit: Elias Most/Caltech
Download Full Image
In a second,
more recent paper in
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
, published March 31 of this year, the team used a supercomputer to simulate what happens after the neutron star fractures—a brief milliseconds-long window when monster shock waves, the most powerful predicted shock waves in the universe, shoot outward from the star. These monster shock waves had only recently been predicted by co-author Andrei Beloborodov of Columbia University. Now, the simulation, along with another from
a different study
published by the team last year, are the first to show how they form.
What is more, the most recent simulation does not stop when the monster shock waves form—it proceeds to show the neutron star being swallowed, which then triggers the creation of an exotic object called a "black hole pulsar."
A classic pulsar is a highly magnetized neutron star that emits beams of radiation, which sweep around like a lighthouse beacon as the star spins on its axis. A black hole pulsar is a hypothetical object in which a black hole launches magnetic winds that would also sweep around it as it spins, mimicking the appearance of a pulsar. While black hole pulsars had been previously conjectured, the simulation is the first to show how such a rare object could actually form in nature from the collision of a neutron star and black hole.
"When the neutron star plunges into the black hole, the monster shock waves are launched," says Yoonsoo Kim (MS '24), a Caltech graduate student working with Most, and lead author of the study on monster shock waves and black hole pulsars. "After the star is sucked in, whipping winds are formed, creating the black hole pulsar. But the black hole cannot sustain its winds and will become quiet again within seconds."

data.article_summary: 本文作者Cube Flipper分享了自己在女性化激素疗法中的个人体验，并讨论了性别不安（gender dysphoria）的感受。作者强调，是否经历性别不安不应成为服用激素的前提，每个人有权选择在自己体内使用何种激素。作者通过自我探索，最终在COVID-19疫情期间通过自我管理的氯胺酮疗法面对自己的性别不安问题，并开始使用雌二醇贴片。文章详细描述了雌激素的生理作用及其对主观体验的影响，虽然其物理效果已有详细记录，但主观报告相对少见。作者还介绍了性激素的基本科学原理，包括不同类型的雌激素及其作用机制。最终，作者通过亲身尝试来验证这种疗法是否适合自己。

主要讨论点：跨性别者的激素替代疗法（HRT）、药物使用的影响以及性别认同的感知差异

不同观点：
• **HRT对情绪和感知的影响**：
   - [DoctorOW] 认为HRT（特别是雌激素）可以减少跨性别者使用娱乐性药物的频率，因为性别欢愉（gender euphoria）带来了持久的幸福感，而不是简单的生理快感。
   - [pazimzadeh] 对描述HRT带来的感知变化感到困惑，认为应该有更简单的方式来解释这些变化。
   - [egypturnash] 表示自己的HRT体验与文章中描述的非常不同，质疑所谓的“激素让跨性别者对世界的感知发生巨大变化”的说法，并指出个人的体验可能因人而异。

• **性别认同与兴趣的关系**：
   - [MondayGravity] 提问跨性别女性是否认为自己拥有“错误的性别”或“错误的身体”，并指出自己认识的跨性别女性仍倾向于男性主导的兴趣，这与通常的性别刻板印象不符。
   - [marcellus23] 延伸讨论了跨性别者在接受激素治疗后感知上的变化，并提问这是否意味着顺性别（cis）男女在感知世界上的差异，例如味觉和颜色的感知。

• **药物使用与身体自主权**：
   - [gherkinnn] 对个人在身体中使用任何物质的权利表示赞同，并认为通过他人的经历来理解不同性别感受是有趣的。
   - [somsak2] 指出在跨性别群体中使用类固醇与在健美圈中的使用被区别对待的现象。
   - [comrade1234] 对在美国无需医生指导即可轻易获取激素表示担忧，认为这可能导致健康问题。

• **HRT与自闭症的关系**：
   - [HK-NC] 提到自闭症与跨性别者之间的关联，认为跨性别现象可能与在子宫中暴露于过量睾酮有关，并提出通过激素疗法来平衡这一现象的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **讨论的质量和氛围**：
   - [titanomachy] 对论坛中关于激素治疗的讨论质量和文明程度表示赞赏。

• **个人经历和体验**：
   - [trenbologna] 分享了自己在高睾酮和高雌激素状态下感觉良好的经历，并认为这给了他窥见女性心理的体验。
   - [calico96] 提供了Lynn Conway关于1960年代雌激素治疗的文档链接，为讨论提供了历史背景。

• **实际操作问题**：
   - [kushan2020] 提问日常饮用能量饮料是否会影响HRT效果，这涉及到实际生活中饮食习惯与激素治疗的相互作用。

• **争议焦点**：
   - 主要集中在HRT对感知和情绪的具体影响以及个体体验的差异，部分人质疑文章中描述的极端感知变化的真实性。
   - 另一个争议点是获取激素的容易程度以及在没有医生指导下的潜在健康风险。

Estrogen: A trip report
Posted on 15 June 2025 by
Cube Flipper
Iâd like to say thanks to
Anna Magpie
â who offers
literature review as a service
â for her help reviewing the
section on neuroendocrinology
.
The following blog post discusses my personal experience of the phenomenology of feminising hormone therapy. It will also touch upon my own experience of gender dysphoria.
I wish to be clear that I do not believe that someone should have to demonstrate that they experience gender dysphoria â
however one might even define that
â as a prerequisite for taking hormones. At
smoothbrains.net
, we hold as self-evident the right to put whatever one likes inside oneâs body; and this of course includes hormones, be they androgens, estrogens, or exotic xenohormones as yet uninvented.
I have
gender dysphoria
. I find labels overly reifying; I feel reluctant to call myself
transgender
, per se: when prompted to state my gender identity or preferred pronouns, I fold my hands into the
dhyana mudra
and state that I
practice
emptiness
on the concept of gender
. Mostly people seem to vibe it, but sometimes it feels a little like weasel words. Other times, when Iâm in a sillier mood, Iâll tell people Iâm
genderfluid
â if only because it sounds like something Iâd put in my station wagon. Of course, my faithful Subaru Outback was made before 2008, which means it wants the
green, long-life genderfluid
â¦
I experience an ongoing
brain-body map
prediction error
â my brain seems to expect a differently shaped body to the one I wound up with. I have been acutely aware of this since before I hit puberty. Out of shame and embarassment, I suppressed this, but I also made a promise to myself that if I hadnât come out by the time I turned thirty then I was allowed to get as weird as I needed to.
During the COVID-19 pandemic I went through a phase of using self-administered ketamine therapy to refactor a long list of maladaptive behavioural patterns, and eventually this particular issue became impossible to ignore. I had avoided reifying it for long enough, and this wasnât working for me â I had to try something different. One evening in July 2021, I sat down with a close friend.
I am going to put a large amount of ketamine up my nose
, I said.
Your job is to start asking me questions about my sexuality.
Not long after, I had jumped through the relevant bureaucratic hoops,
and subsequently found myself cycling home from the pharmacy with a paper bag filled with repurposed menopause medication â a starter pack of
100 Âµg/24 hr
estradiol patches, to be applied twice a week.
While the
physical
effects of estrogen are
well-documented
, back when I came out I had difficulty finding detailed phenomenological reports of the
subjective
effects of estrogen. I did wind up reading a large number of anecdotal reports on
Reddit
, and found that in aggregate, people tend to report
positive subjective effects
. One could propose a number of non-exclusive hypotheses as to why â Iâll attempt to review these later in this post.
Did it make sense for me to try this? It was time to find out for myself. I unboxed the patches and placed one on my stomach.
It bears mentioning that I have tried a high testosterone lifestyle before, so itâs not as if I was entering into this from a state of hormonal deficiency. In my late twenties I started cycling every day, lost a ton of weight, and learned how to deadlift. I neglected to have my hormone levels checked, but if itâs any indication, my biceps got swole and my chest hair suddenly grew quite thick and curly. This felt good in its own right, but did not fix the dysphoria.
What does estrogen
do
?
The
sex hormones
â
androgens
,
estrogens
, and
progestogens
â are produced by the
endocrine system
. They are released into the bloodstream in response to a range of regulatory factors â primarily the
hypothalamicâpituitaryâgonadal axis
â as a signal for distant cells to regulate a wide variety of bodily functions.
To be clear, there are four major endogenous estrogens â
estrone
,
estradiol
,
estriol
, and
estetrol
â though estetrol is only produced during pregnancy. Most modern feminising hormone therapy involves application of estradiol. However, there do exist other estrogens â including
17Î±-estradiol
, noteworthy for being non-feminising while also extending the lifespan of male mice. There are also other compounds with estrogenic activity, for example the
androstanediols
.
At the other end,
receptors
are â very generally speaking â a class of proteins which can
change their shape
when
specific molecules
bind to them. Of these,
estrogen receptors
are primarily
nuclear receptors
, although a smaller fraction of them are
cell surface receptors
. These are typically located in the cellâs
cytoplasm
â but when activated, they pass through the
nuclear membrane
, bind directly to DNA, and
regulate the expression of specific genes
. For comparison,

data.title: Extracting memorized pieces of books from open-weight language models
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）是否以及如何记忆受版权保护的书籍内容，并对其在版权案件中的影响进行了分析。作者使用了一种概率提取技术，从13个开放权重的LLM中提取了Books3数据集的部分内容。实验表明，部分LLM确实记忆了书籍的 substantial 部分，尤其是像Llama 3.1 70B几乎完整记忆了《哈利·波特》和《1984》等书籍。然而，最大型的LLM并没有显著记忆大多数书籍。文章指出，这一发现对版权案件具有重要意义，但并不单一地偏向任何一方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLM）与版权法的争议

不同观点：
• iamleppert认为，科技公司已经积累了大量权力并深度投入于AI，法律判决更多依赖于解释者的偏见和动机，而非纯粹的法律条文。即使存在不合理或牵强的辩护理由，也可能会在长期的法律斗争中获胜。

• ai_legal_sus指出，训练数据中包含版权材料是公开的秘密，问题在于LLM的输出是否构成“实质性相似”。他们认为用户为访问压缩的训练数据付费，如果输出侵犯版权，LLM服务应该承担责任。

• Animats质疑LLM是否能生成可恢复训练数据的书籍列表，并提出是否仅因《哈利·波特》等书籍有大量粉丝材料而显得重要。

• Huxley1认为LLM不仅仅是死记硬背，而是压缩和重组内容，版权问题复杂且法律需要适应这些新技术。

• jrm4强调，如果将作品放入LLM，它可以生成可识别的副本，即使看不见副本的存在也无关紧要，这构成了版权侵权。

• andy99提出两个可能构成版权侵权的点：一是使用盗版材料训练LLM，二是用户使用LLM生成侵犯版权的内容。训练本身不构成侵权，且LLM已被加强以防止生成侵权内容。

• landl0rd补充，LLM“记住”热门书籍是因为这些书籍的引用在训练集中高度代表，大多数情况下只是合理使用。

• w10-1认为，将版权法应用于AI是误导的，版权侵权本质上是盗窃行为。尽管现有法律不明确，但从原则上讲，购买书籍并不包括自动手段处理文本以进行回忆或复制的权利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM是否以及如何侵犯版权，特别是在训练数据包含版权材料的情况下，用户生成的输出是否构成侵权。
• 讨论还涉及法律如何适应新技术，以及现有版权法的适用性和局限性。

Title:
Extracting memorized pieces of (copyrighted) books from open-weight language models
Authors:
A. Feder Cooper
,
Aaron Gokaslan
,
Amy B. Cyphert
,
Christopher De Sa
,
Mark A. Lemley
,
Daniel E. Ho
,
Percy Liang
View a PDF of the paper titled Extracting memorized pieces of (copyrighted) books from open-weight language models, by A. Feder Cooper and Aaron Gokaslan and Amy B. Cyphert and Christopher De Sa and Mark A. Lemley and Daniel E. Ho and Percy Liang
View PDF
Abstract:
Plaintiffs and defendants in copyright lawsuits over generative AI often make sweeping, opposing claims about the extent to which large language models (LLMs) have memorized plaintiffs' protected expression. Drawing on adversarial ML and copyright law, we show that these polarized positions dramatically oversimplify the relationship between memorization and copyright. To do so, we leverage a recent probabilistic extraction technique to extract pieces of the Books3 dataset from 13 open-weight LLMs. Through numerous experiments, we show that it's possible to extract substantial parts of at least some books from different LLMs. This is evidence that the LLMs have memorized the extracted text; this memorized content is copied inside the model parameters. But the results are complicated: the extent of memorization varies both by model and by book. With our specific experiments, we find that the largest LLMs don't memorize most books -- either in whole or in part. However, we also find that Llama 3.1 70B memorizes some books, like Harry Potter and 1984, almost entirely. We discuss why our results have significant implications for copyright cases, though not ones that unambiguously favor either side.

• andy99提出两个可能构成版权侵权的点：一是使用盗版材料训练LLM，二是用户使用LLM生成侵犯版权的内容。训练本身不构成侵权，且LLM已被加强以防止生成侵权内容。

• landl0rd补充，LLM“记住”热门书籍是因为这些书籍的引用在训练集中高度代表，大多数情况下只是合理使用。

• w10-1认为，将版权法应用于AI是误导的，版权侵权本质上是盗窃行为。尽管现有法律不明确，但从原则上讲，购买书籍并不包括自动手段处理文本以进行回忆或复制的权利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM是否以及如何侵犯版权，特别是在训练数据包含版权材料的情况下，用户生成的输出是否构成侵权。
• 讨论还涉及法律如何适应新技术，以及现有版权法的适用性和局限性。

data.title: Double-Entry Ledgers: The Missing Primitive in Modern Software
data.author: pgr0ss
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了双 entries 记账模型在软件开发中的未充分利用，并介绍了一个名为 "pgledger" 的纯 PostgreSQL 实现。双 entries 记账包含几个核心概念：当前余额、余额变化的历史记录以及资金来源。这种模型通过原子性的记录确保数据的一致性和错误检查，同时提供审计日志功能。

文章以在线业务为例，展示了如何使用双 entries 记账来记录订单、付款和退款。通过这种方法，可以明确记录每个资金转移，并方便地回答如“我们还在等多少钱？”或“为什么余额不对？”等问题。相比传统单表记录方式，双 entries 记账能更清晰地追踪资金流动，减少自定义错误检查逻辑的需要。

总的来说，文章提倡在更多系统中使用双 entries 记账，以提高数据一致性和可追溯性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： ledger（账本）系统的实际应用及其技术挑战，尤其是在处理大量交易记录时如何高效获取特定账户在特定时间的余额。

不同观点：
• accrual：认为账本不仅适用于个人会计，还有许多其他实际应用场景。同时提出，当交易记录达到百万甚至上亿级别时，如何高效获取某个时间点的账户余额是一个问题。他建议通过将账本划分为"完成"或"封印"的组，并设置"检查点"来优化计算。

• GianFabien：基于实际项目经验，指出每个账本系统几乎都有其独特之处，尤其是涉及多种货币和不同汇率合同时，计算当前余额非常复杂。他还提到旧时的"封账"做法，类似于accrual提到的"检查点"概念，可以作为解决方案之一。

• euroderf：简单提及技术实现问题，表示如果SQLite支持WASM UDFs（WebAssembly用户自定义函数），可能会对解决账本技术问题有所帮助，但没有展开具体讨论。

补充讨论：
• accrual和GianFabien都认识到处理大量交易记录时，直接计算余额可能会导致性能问题，并分别提出了"检查点"和"封账"的概念来解决这一问题。
• GianFabien通过实际案例强调了多货币和复杂汇率合同对账本系统的额外挑战。
• euroderf的评论暗示了技术工具的局限性，并暗示了可能的改进方向，但没有详细展开。

争议焦点：如何在账本系统中高效计算大量交易记录的余额，尤其是在复杂应用场景下（如多货币、多种汇率合同）。

I think ledgers are underutilized in software development today. Specifically,
double-entry ledger
modeling would be a better fit in a lot of systems than the ad-hoc ledger-ish things they currently have.
This is why Iâve been working on
pgledger
, a pure PostgreSQL ledger implementation. If adding a ledger implementation is super simple, then Iâm hoping more folks will do it. And it can become another modeling primitive that we reach for to accomplish all sorts of things.
What is a Ledger?
A double-entry ledger at its core is a few simple concepts put together:
The current amount or balance of a thing
A historical record of how the amount got to that amount (immutable, append only, etc)
Where that amount came from at each step
Thatâs it. So if Alice sends $100 to Bob, the ledger records Aliceâs balance changing from $0 to $-100 (going to Bob) and Bobâs balance changing from $0 to $100 (coming from Alice). All of this is recorded at once, all amounts are accounted for, and all balances sum to $0.
Note:
Many ledgers model debits and credits rather than negative and positive numbers. In this case, Alice would have a debit of $100 and Bob would have a credit of $100. Personally, I find using negative and positive numbers simpler.
1
The fact that every transfer only moves amounts, never creates them from scratch, is a built-in error check.
2
And the historical record serves as an audit log.
How the ledger is implemented and what is actually stored on disk varies with each ledger implementation, but the important point is that all of this information is recorded atomically.
Once you start thinking about tracking amount changes over time, you start seeing ledgers in more places. Letâs walk through some examples Iâve seen in real software.
Recording Payments
Say we are building an online business. Starting simple, we need to know when someone places an order, so maybe we start with an
orders
table. But then we realize that payments have a more complicated lifecycle (we donât receive the payment right away when an order is created), so we want to know when we can actually start service or ship a product. We might add a
payments
table with a
status
column that represents values like
waiting_to_receive
or
complete
.
This is sort of like a single entry ledger. We have a table of âtransfersâ from customers to our business. But things soon get more complicated. How do we record a refund? Is that a new
refunds
table? Or do we record a row in
payments
with a negative amount? What happens when our account balance isnât what we expect? Are we missing payments? Or did we receive a different amount than we expected? How can we figure it out?
If we have a real double-entry ledger, we can record these interactions more explicitly:
When an order is created, we now have a
receivable
, where we are waiting on money. We can represent this as a transfer from the external user to a
receivables

Then, when we actually receive the money in our account, we can move it from the

available

If it isnât, something went wrong, such as receiving less than we expected. With the original modeling, weâd have to build something custom to check the received amount against what we expected. We can also easily answer questions like âhow much money are we waiting for?â without any extra logic (the balance of the
receivables
account).
Or if we donât have the balance we expect, itâs easier to figure out why. We can look at the entries for an account and see every balance change over time and look for discrepancies. We can also look at other balances and see how they relate. Maybe our bank balance is $100 lower than we expect, but a different account is $100 more than we expect. data.title: Show HN: I wrote a new BitTorrent tracker in Elixir
data.author: dahrkael
data.article_summary: ExTracker 是一个使用 Elixir 开发的 BitTorrent Tracker，目前仍在开发中，但已具备一些功能。它具有高性能、低内存占用、零配置等特点，支持 UDP 协议、IPv6 扩展、BitTorrent v2 协议等。部分功能如私有种子和 WebTorrent 尚未实现。项目提供了三种运行方式：源码运行、通过 Releases 部署和使用 Docker。ExTracker 遵循 Apache-2.0 许可证，由 Dahrkael 开发和维护。目前有一个测试实例在运行，支持实时统计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir实现的Torrent Tracker项目及其设计与功能

不同观点：
• [TheJoeMan] 对DHT和PEX的含义感到困惑，寻求澄清，特别是关于"tracker PEX"的资料。
• [nesarkvechnep] 希望看到以OTP（Open Telecom Platform）为核心的设计，而不是目前这种接近过程式的代码，并推荐了两本相关的书籍以帮助改进设计。
• [voicedYoda] 对项目表示赞赏，但建议使用专业的日志系统替代IO.puts，并考虑加入OTel（OpenTelemetry）以增强可观测性。
• [arch-choot] 分享了自己用Typescript和Rust实现类似项目的经验，特别是使用了Redis作为数据库，并对全部数据放在内存中的设计提出疑问。
• [quechimba] 提到自己几年前用Elixir写过类似的Tracker，并分享了代码链接供参考。

补充讨论：
• [abrookewood] 对项目与opentracker的性能比较表示关注，希望了解更多细节。
• [s-mon] 表达了对Elixir的喜爱，并提到自己正在用Elixir构建通知引擎。
• [vivzkestrel] 提出了一系列关于项目开发过程的问题，包括项目启动方式、参考项目、开发时间以及与qbittorrent的功能比较。
• [KomoD] 在使用中遇到HTTPS无法工作的问题，并提到控制台被无效参数警告刷屏，同时表达了对HTTP统计功能的需求。
• [jhgg] 对项目作者是否考虑将Elixir作为主要工作表示好奇。
• [IlikeKitties] 认为Beam VM（Elixir运行的虚拟机）非常适合用于Torrent Tracker项目。
• [bavell] 询问该项目是否适合用作私人Tracker。
• [toomuchtodo] 和 [mikehostetler] 对项目表示赞赏和祝贺。
• [desireco42] 对项目的实现表示认可，并认为Elixir非常适合这种应用场景。

争议焦点：
- 项目设计是否应更多采用OTP模式，而非当前接近过程式的设计。
- 全部数据放在内存中的设计决策及其潜在问题。
- HTTPS无法工作及控制台警告问题，显示出项目在功能完善性上的不足。

Setup
There are 3 main ways of running ExTracker currently
Straight from source code
For this method to work you need to have
Erlang
and
Elixir
installed on your system
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/Dahrkael/ExTracker.git && cd ExTracker
If needed, modify the configuration in
config/runtime.exs
to fit your needs
run
MIX_ENV=prod iex -S mix
From Releases
Currently there are no official releases built (soon™️). You can however make your own and deploy it where needed:
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/Dahrkael/ExTracker.git && cd ExTracker
run
MIX_ENV=prod mix release extracker
for Linux or
MIX_ENV=prod mix release extrackerw
for Windows
Find the release files inside the
_build/prod/rel/extracker
folder (if its a different machine make sure the OS and architecture is the same!)
Copy the folder to its final destination
If needed, modify the configuration in
releases/{VERSION}/runtime.exs
to fit your needs
Run
bin/extracker start
Docker
For this method you can directly run the
available docker image
:
docker run ghcr.io/dahrkael/extracker:latest
or use it as part of docker-compose. Theres an
example compose file
available.
Note
Since modifying the
runtime.exs
file to tune the configuration inside the container is not easy you can also configure it using
Environment Variables
, see the example compose file for the complete list.

data.article_summary: "Literate" 是一个用于文学编程的工具，旨在创建易于理解和分享的程序。文学编程由Donald Knuth提出，强调代码首先是给人读的，其次才是给计算机执行的。Literate程序通常包含自然语言（如英语）解释和代码片段。"Literate" 工具支持任意编程语言，具有语法高亮、Markdown编写、错误报告、生成可读代码和HTML、支持TeX公式、自动生成超链接等功能。它还提供快速编译和高度自定义的输出。用户可以通过预构建二进制文件或从源代码构建来安装该工具，并支持Micro和Vim编辑器。通过命令行使用，可以生成代码文件和HTML文件，并提供多种选项以满足不同需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Literate Programming（文学编程）的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• **反对观点（Mikhail_Edoshin）**：认为文学编程并不是好的文档方式。文档应该正式且有标准结构，而不是依赖文学编程的灵活性。文学编程过于“狡猾”，虽然强调了文档的重要性，但其方式并不理想。例如，METAFONT的文档虽然详尽，但其代码和具体语言（Pascal）绑定，不利于跨语言理解。
• **支持观点（bilalq）**：通过个人经验表明文学编程有助于项目的长期可读性，特别是在回顾多年前的代码时，文学编程能让项目更易于理解，提供了代码背后的上下文信息，即使代码本身已经清晰。
• **工具推荐（txgvnn & amanwithnoplan）**：推荐使用Emacs的org-mode和Entangled等工具来实现文学编程，这些工具能够很好地处理文学编程中的文档与代码的交互。
• **实践经验（svieira & tony_cannistra）**：提到实际的文学编程项目案例，如Literate和noweb，展示了文学编程在实际项目中的应用及其吸引力。
• **AI与文学编程（jostylr）**：探讨AI编码工具可能使文学编程再次变得有价值，特别是在代码审查和验证过程中。

补充讨论：
• **文学编程的局限性（seanwilson & mapcars）**：质疑文学编程是否适用于大型项目，特别是当代码和文档难以保持同步时。现代IDE提供的功能（如语法高亮、实时类型检查）在文学编程环境中可能不足。
• **特定场景的优势（nothrabannosir）**：认为文学编程在shell脚本等场景中具有优势，特别是在需要高文档需求的代码中，文学编程能够很好地处理外部链接和文档化的实验过程。
• **工具的现状与发展（kstrauser）**：关注文学编程工具的更新情况，质疑其是否已经成熟或被弃用，并询问当前社区中常用的替代工具。
• **简洁的观点（stevelini & asimpletune）**：有人认为文学编程的示例（如300行实现word count）可能过于复杂，而另一种观点则强调阅读代码比写代码更重要，暗示文学编程在这方面有其独特价值。

争议焦点：
• 文学编程是否优于传统文档和注释方式，特别是在代码同步和大型项目中的可操作性。
• 现代开发环境对文学编程的支持程度，以及是否需要专门的IDE来实现其优势。

Literate
What is Literate programming?
Literate programming is a style of programming invented by Donald Knuth, where the main idea is that a program's source code is made primarily to be read and understood by other people, and secondarily to be executed by the computer.
This frees the programmer from the structure of a program imposed by the computer and means that the programmer can develop programs in the order of the flow of their thoughts.
A Literate program generally consists of explanation of the code in a natural language such as English, interspersed with snippets of code to be executed. This means that Literate programs are very easy to understand and share, as all the code is well explained.
Literate is a tool for creating literate programs.
The goal of this project is to create a literate programming tool which keeps most, if not all of the features of Knuth and Levy's original CWEB system, but simplifies the system and adds even more features.
You can view the main website about Literate
here
including a
manual
on how to use Literate.
Features
Supports any language including syntax highlighting and pretty printing in HTML
Markdown based -- very easy to read and write Literate source.
Reports syntax errors back from the compiler to the right line in the literate source
Generates readable and commented code in the target language (the generated code is usable by others)
Supports TeX equations with
$
notation.
Literate source code is readable whether you are looking at the
.lit
file, or the generated HTML.
Highly customizable (you can add your own HTML or CSS)
Runs fast -- wc.lit compiled for me in 7ms for both code and HTML output
Automatically generates hyperlinks between code sections
Formatted output similar to CWEB
Supported by
micro
(by default)
Compatible with Vim (
literate.vim
)
Example
Here is a trivial example of a literate program saved in the file
hello.lit
.
For a full example of a literate program, please see
examples/wc.lit
which
is a literate implementation of the
wc
(word count) program found on Unix systems.
You can find the compiled html
here
.
@title Hello world in C
@s Introduction
This is an example hello world C program.
We can define codeblocks with `---`
--- hello.c
@{Includes}
int main() {
@{Print a string}
return 0;
}
---
Now we can define the `Includes` codeblock:
--- Includes
#include <stdio.h>
---
Finally, our program needs to print "hello world"
--- Print a string
printf("hello world\n");
---
To compile this code simply run
$ lit hello.lit
Which generates
hello.c
and
hello.html
.
You can also find this program in
examples/hello.lit
.
Installation
Prebuilt binaries
Download
Mac OS X
64 bit Linux
32 bit Linux
Arm Linux
Building from Source
Mac
On Mac you can use brew to build Literate from source:
$ brew tap zyedidia/literate
$ brew install --HEAD literate
For now, Literate is head only.
Literate is made with the
D programming language
so you must install
dmd
(D compiler) and
dub
(D package manager). Then you should download the zip or clone the repository and run the following commands:
$ cd Literate
$ make
You can find the binary in path/to/Literate/bin (you may want to add this to your path or move it to
/usr/local/bin
).
Editors
Micro
The micro editor has support for literate by default. Download it
here
.
Vim
You might also want to go install the
Vim plugin
(it has syntax highlighting of the embedded code, linting with Neomake, and jumping to codeblock definitions).
I'm sorry that no other editors are supported -- I don't know how to make plugins for other editors.
Usage
Lit: Literate Programming System
Usage: lit [options] <inputs>
Options:
--help       -h         Show this help text
--tangle     -t         Only compile code files
--weave      -w         Only compile HTML files
--no-output  -no        Do not generate any output files
--out-dir    -odir DIR  Put the generated files in DIR
--compiler   -c         Report compiler errors (needs @compiler to be defined)
--linenums   -l    STR  Write line numbers prepended with STR to the output file
--md-compiler COMPILER  Use COMPILER as the markdown compiler instead of the built-in one
--version    -v         Show the version number and compiler information
For more information see the
manual
.

data.title: Show HN: RM2000 Tape Recorder, an audio sampler for macOS
data.author: marcelox86
data.article_summary: RM2000 Tape Recorder是一款用于Mac的录音软件，可将你的Mac变成采样器，快速录制灵感。它能即时录制系统播放的任何声音，无需复杂的音频路由或第三方工具。软件操作简便，无需设置，录制后可轻松归档、标记和组织音频。它采用“文件优先于应用”的理念，支持在不同应用中使用录制的样本。该软件通过App Store下载，提供一次性终身许可证，当前促销价为6.99美元，并有免费试用期，优惠截止于6月30日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RM2000 Tape Recorder应用的功能、使用体验、隐私问题及技术细节

不同观点：
• arkwin提到应用后台运行时，全局录制功能存在保存文件时没有弹出提示的bug，并询问该问题是否会在1.0.2版本中修复。
• asdhtjkujh对应用的设计表示赞赏，并希望增加全局快捷键功能，以便在全屏观看视频时录制环境音频，类似于截屏功能。
• mastazi对录音隐私问题表示关注，询问是否仅在用户明确录制时才会保存音频，确保没有缓存捕捉前几分钟音频的功能。
• JodieBenitez表示对应用感兴趣，但由于所在国家不可用，无法购买。
• pdntspa对从YouTube采样并拖入Ableton的演示视频表示不满，认为这会导致音频质量损失。
• marcelox1986回复了关于1.0.1版本中样本保存不当的bug，并告知1.0.2版本已修复并等待App Store审核。

• lagniappe简短表达了对Oneohtrix Point Never的喜欢。
• mmmnnn分享了一个类似的音频工具链接（https://existential.audio/blackhole/）。
• chaosprint对UI设计表示赞赏，并分享了自己以前制作的网页采样Chrome插件链接。
• randomsofr喜欢UI设计，但指出应用官网在最新版Chrome和MacOS上加载速度较慢。
• quesera注意到网站使用了Garamond字体，表示感慨。
• mjcohen询问该应用与Audio Hijack在录音功能上的比较。

补充讨论：
• 用户对应用的UI设计普遍表示赞赏，但也存在对应用名和设计元素的质疑。
• 技术问题包括后台录制bug、音频缓存隐私问题、国家区域限制以及音频质量损失等。
• 一些用户分享了类似工具和个人项目，丰富了讨论内容。
• 争议焦点主要在于应用命名的准确性及录音功能的细节实现，比如是否模拟磁带效果。

data.title: Octobass
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: The octobass is an extremely rare and massive musical instrument, standing nearly 12 feet tall and invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume. It produces incredibly low-pitched sounds, some beyond human hearing, and is played using pedals and levers due to its large size and thick strings. Only seven known examples exist, with one housed in the Musical Instrument Museum in Phoenix, Arizona. Originally requiring two people to play, it is now usually managed by one. The Montreal Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra to own an octobass, and it is rarely featured in compositions. Visitors to the museum can see the octobass for a $20 admission fee.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Octobass的构造、使用及其独特性

不同观点：
• **garthogjazz** 指出文章中展示的octobass并不完整，缺少了Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume设计的踏板，这些踏板能实现连奏（legato），而仅使用杠杆是无法实现的。他还提到蒙特利尔共有三台Octobass，其中一台是原版的复制品（有些许升级），另外两台是由马达驱动的。

• **jclem** 分享了一个与朋友在跨海岸软件调试时互相发送octobass调音图片的趣事，特别提到在开发实时协作文本编辑器时尤为相关。

• **PaulHoule** 讲述了他的儿子在开始弹奏吉他和贝斯后，热衷于制作乐器，将乌克丽丽和无品吉他结合，并在一把吉他上安装了两个琴桥，使其具有竖琴部分。他的儿子还询问了关于制造比普通贝斯低一到两个八度的电贝斯的物理原理。

• **kjgkjhfkjf** 提供了一个octobass演奏视频的链接，虽然演奏并不完全专业。

• **apricot** 纠正了关于蒙特利尔交响乐团拥有唯一一台octobass的说法，指出他们实际上有三台。

• **leptons** 推荐了菲尼克斯的乐器博物馆，认为这是该地最佳旅游活动之一，也是他最喜欢的博物馆之一。

• **BoostandEthanol** 对文章中提到的“有些乐器的声音低于人类听觉范围，只能感觉到振动”感到难以置信，认为在这种功率下不可能只感受到振动而听不到声音。

• **JKCalhoun** 回忆起在菲尼克斯见过这台高大的贝斯，并称赞菲尼克斯是一个有趣的城市，推荐了植物园作为必去景点。

About
Composers and orchestras like to use their lowest instruments sparingly, for maximum impact. Few instruments go lower and are used more sparingly than the huge and strange octobass, one of the rarest classic instruments in existence.
Invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume, the octobass was intended to bring an extremely deep rumble to the orchestra sound. The three-stringed instrument stands between 11 and 12 feet tall, about twice the height of a double bass. This giant bass produces sound so low, some of the notes fall outside the range of human hearing—these vibrations can only be felt.
The rare instrument is almost too large to play. The strings are too big to press with your fingers, so fretting them requires operating pedals and levers that control capo-like mechanisms to press down the strings. In fact, the octobass originally required two people to play: one on the bow (which, though shorter that the bow of a double bass, is extra heavy) and one working the lever system.
Vuillaume originally built three octobasses, two of which are still around. Including contemporary, playable replicas, there are only seven known examples of the instrument in the world, mostly kept in museums, including one at the Musical Instrument Museum in
Phoenix
,
Arizona
. The octobass in Phoenix is tuned C0, G0, D1, a range that's two octaves below the cello and one octave below the modern double bass. Its low C note is lower than the lowest note on an 88-key piano, and beyond what most people can hear (
you can give it a listen here
).
The
Montreal
Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra that owns one of these unusual instruments, and composers still write music for it on occasion. When played today, it is usually by a single person.

It's part of the collection at the Musical Instrument Museum. To see the Octobass you will have to pay a $20 admission fee for the museum. Prepare for long lines to get into the museum. Budget at least two hours to see all of the exhibits.

44288595.article_summary: The octobass is an extremely rare and massive musical instrument, standing nearly 12 feet tall and invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume. It produces incredibly low-pitched sounds, some beyond human hearing, and is played using pedals and levers due to its large size and thick strings. Only seven known examples exist, with one housed in the Musical Instrument Museum in Phoenix, Arizona. Originally requiring two people to play, it is now usually managed by one. The Montreal Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra to own an octobass, and it is rarely featured in compositions. Visitors to the museum can see the octobass for a $20 admission fee.

data.title: FedFlix — Public Domain Stock Footage Library
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了美国国家技术信息服务局（NTIS）与Public.Resource.Org（PRO）之间的一项联合项目，旨在促进公众获取NTIS馆藏中的多媒体产品。根据协议，NTIS每月将选取10至20盘非版权录像带寄给PRO，PRO负责将其数字化并制作成DVD拷贝，随后返还NTIS。所有内容均为美国政府财产，双方均可自由通过任何形式向公众提供这些内容并保留全部收入。协议有效期为一年，可提前60天通知终止。PRO对内容不享有知识产权，且NTIS可将内容提供给其他合作伙伴。该项目的内容也可在Internet Archive上获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FedFlix目录浏览器的使用及相关资源的质量和命名建议

不同观点：
• [jchrisa] 对FedFlix API的肯定，认为其易于使用，并分享了一个快速创建的目录浏览器链接。他还鼓励其他人通过“remix”按钮进行自定义。
• [mrbluecoat] 对FedFlix内容命名提出幽默批评，认为像"The Great Seal of the Seal of Approval"这样的标题错失了命名为"Nedflix"的机会，暗示命名的创意不足。
• [pogue] 对FedFlix资源质量提出质疑，认为目前看到的多是低分辨率的短片，并询问是否有值得使用的如旧B卷或二战 footage等资源。

补充讨论：
• [blensor] 提出一个与主讨论稍微偏离的观点，建议创建一个包含自由使用的AI生成视频和歌曲的图书馆，认为这样可以节省能源并提高生成内容的利用率。这一观点引出了对资源浪费和内容生成准确性的关注。

争议焦点：
- FedFlix资源命名的创意不足（[mrbluecoat]的观点）与实际内容的价值（[pogue]的观点）形成了一定的争议，反映出对内容命名和质量的不同期望。

Each month NTIS will select between ten and twenty non-copyrighted videotapes from available stock in its collection and ship them to PRO at its own expense.

PRO will reimburse NTIS for the retail value of any videotape not returned to NTIS as provided in section 2.
Each party is free to make the content of the videotape available to the public through a web site or other means in any format and at any price, or for free, and to retain 100% of the revenue from any sales of the content.
PRO will assert no intellectual property claim to the content provided by NTIS or the resulting DVD in any manner whatsoever.
Nothing in this joint venture purports to be an exclusive arrangement. NTIS may provide content in its videotape collection, including content digitized by PRO under this agreement, to any other business partner.
Unless renewed earlier, this joint venture will terminate one year from the date of execution, except that either party may terminate it with 60 days written notice to the other. If NTIS terminates, PRO may either return any videotapes it has not yet digitized at NTIS' expense or it may treat those videotapes as subject to section 4. If PRO terminates, it may either return any videotapes not yet digitized at its own expense or it may treat those videotapes as subject to section 4.
Neither party may assign its rights under this Agreement to a third party without the written consent of the other party.

data.title: Infinite Mac OS X
data.author: kristianp
data.article_summary: Infinite Mac现在支持运行早期的Mac OS X，特别是10.1和10.3版本。尽管速度不快，但在实际硬件上表现也差不多。Infinite HD也更新加入了那个时代的知名独立软件。文章还讨论了通过PearPC模拟器在Infinite Mac上运行Mac OS X的过程。作者尝试了多种模拟器，最终通过PearPC成功实现，并对其进行了WebAssembly/Emscripten移植。虽然PearPC运行更稳定，但性能不如DingusPPC，主要瓶颈在于缺乏MMU缓存。最终，作者在UI中添加了启动缓慢的提示，并继续优化模拟器以提升性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对旧款Mac操作系统及相关技术（如PearPC、Infinite Mac）的回顾与评价

不同观点：
• [donatj, kristianp] 提到PearPC项目在早期取得了一定成功，但由于核心开发者去世和兴趣减退，项目逐渐失去动力。PearPC的代码库目前处于停滞状态，但仍有部分分支和WebAssembly目标的支持。
• [treve, cbeach] 分享了Infinite Mac项目，该项目允许用户通过浏览器体验经典的Macintosh和NeXT系统。用户对能够在现代浏览器中重温旧时UI感到兴奋，并提到具体游戏（如Dark Castle）的体验，唤起了怀旧情感。
• [WoodenChair] 对PPC CPU模拟器代码的简洁性表示赞赏，认为这种简洁性在相对现代的架构中不常见，通常只在6502等老式架构中见到。
• [papaver-somnamb] 对过去的UI设计表示怀念，认为过去的UI元素更加一致、可预测，而现代UI虽然可定制和更"酷"，但可能缺乏一致性。
• [thomassmith65] 对现代年轻技术爱好者面对旧版操作系统（如OS X 10.4）可能产生的感受进行了哲学性思考，将之比作站在古典雕塑前的中世纪人，表达了对过去美好事物的怀念。
• [TekMol] 认为旧版Mac OS X的界面设计优于当前版本，当前版本的界面过于花哨，影响了工作效率。
• [wk_end] 认为OS X早期是Mac的黄金时代，硬件和操作系统都非常出色。虽然现在硬件再次进入黄金时代，但期望操作系统也能再次达到巅峰。
• [hobofan] 以Hackintosh用户的经历支持早期OS X性能不佳的说法，并提到过去的安装和使用过程非常耗时。

补充讨论：
• [plun9] 对Aqua界面在当时的革命性表示赞赏。
• [lavelett36] 对Infinite Mac项目的介绍文章表示困惑，认为文章没有清晰解释项目的性质和使用方法，对于不熟悉相关术语的用户不友好。
• [Bjartr] 提到systemd的流行与它违背经典Unix哲学有关，暗示技术发展中功能性和哲学性之间的权衡。

争议焦点：
• 对现代UI设计与过去UI设计的优劣存在不同看法。部分用户认为过去的UI更一致、可预测，而现代UI过于花哨，影响了使用体验。
• 对Infinite Mac项目的介绍不够清晰，导致部分用户不理解项目的性质和使用方法。

44323719.article_content:
tl;dr:
Infinite Mac can now
run early Mac OS X
, with
10.1
and
10.3
being the best supported versions. It’s not particularly snappy, but as someone who lived through that period, I can tell you that it wasn’t much better on real hardware. Infinite HD has also been rebuilt to have some notable indie software from that era.
Porting PearPC
I’ve been
tracking
DingusPPC progress since my initial
port
and making the occasional contribution
myself
, with the hope of using it to run Mac OS X in Infinite Mac. While it has continued to improve, I reached a plateau last summer; my attempts would result in either kernel panics or graphical corruption. I tried to reduce the problem a bit via a
deterministic execution mode
, but it wasn’t really clear where to go next. I decided to take a break from this emulator and explore alternate paths of getting Mac OS X to run.
PearPC
was the obvious choice – it was created with the express purpose of emulating Mac OS X on x86 Windows and Linux machines in the early 2000s. By
all accounts
, it did this successfully for a few years, until interest waned after the Intel switch. I had earlier
dismissed it
as a “dead” codebase, but I decided that the satisfaction of getting something working compensated for dealing with legacy C++ (complete with its own
string class
,
sprintf implementation
, and
GIF decoder
). An encouraging discovery was that
kanjitalk755
(the de-facto Basilisk II and SheepShaver maintainer) had somewhat recently set up
an experimental branch
of PearPC that built and ran on modern macOS. I was able to replicate their work without too much trouble, and with that existence proof I started on my sixth port of an emulator to WebAssembly/Emscripten and the Infinite Mac runtime.
In some ways PearPC not being actively developed made things easier – I didn’t have to worry about merging in changes from upstream, or agonize over how to structure my modifications to make them easier to contribute back. It was also helpful that PearPC was already a multi-platform codebase and thus had the right layers of abstraction to make adding another target pretty easy. As a bonus, it didn’t make pervasive use of threads or other harder-to-port concepts. Over the course of a few days, I was able to
get it to build
,
output video
,
load disk images
, and
get mouse and keyboard input
hooked up. It was pretty satisfying to have Mac OS X 10.2 running in a browser more reliably than it previously had.
Performance
While PearPC ran 10.2 more reliably, it felt slower than DingusPCC. I had spent some time last year making
some
optimizations
to the latter, partly inspired by the
TinyPPC emulator
in
this SheepShaver fork
(aren’t all these names fun?). I
ported
DingusPPC’s benchmark harness and then
set
about
replicating
the
performance
work
in
PearPC
(both emulators are pure interpreters driven by a lookup table, so the process was relatively straightforward). I was able to shave off about 15 seconds from the 10.2 boot time – it helps from a
saving lives perspective
, but is still not enough given that it takes almost 2 minutes to be fully operational. In the end, I copped out and
added a UI disclaimer
that Mac OS X can be slow to boot. I also got flashbacks to the
“is it snappy yet?”
discussions from the early days of Mac OS X – it was indeed slow, but not this slow.
Performance is still not as good as DingusPPC’s – the biggest bottleneck is the lack of any kind of caching in the MMU, so all loads and stores are expensive since they involve complex address computations. DingusPPC has a much more mature
tiered cache
that appears to be quite effective. More generally, while PearPC may be more stable than DingusPPC at running 10.2-10.4, it’s a much less principled codebase (I came across
many mystery commits
) and it “cheats” in many ways (it has a
custom
firmware and
video driver
, and only the
subset
of PowerPC instructions that are needed for Mac OS X are implemented). I’m still holding out hope for DingusPPC to be the fast, stable, and correct choice for the long term.
A Side Quest

主要讨论点：围绕Rubin天文台及其影响的讨论，包括其科学价值、技术挑战和潜在限制。

不同观点：
• **Rubin天文台的科学价值**：ddahlen强调Rubin将极大扩展我们对小行星带的了解，尤其是小行星的数量和种类。通过与NEOS的互补，Rubin将帮助填补小行星目录的空白，特别是在主带区域。
• **技术成就和速度**：asinno将Rubin的速度和MRI扫描的优化相比较，认为其周期性观测具有很高的科学价值。IAmBroom对Rubin的“高速”表示惊叹，特别提到其“最高速度”的测试结果。
• **Starlink的影响和管理**：jl6讨论了Starlink卫星对天文观测的干扰问题，但指出Rubin的多次快速曝光特性可以在一定程度上缓解这种影响。

补充讨论：
• **Rubin与其他项目的关系**：ddahlen提到NEOS，这是一项红外望远镜项目，能够弥补Rubin在观测暗物质小行星方面的不足。
• **技术细节和未来设想**：viraptor提出关于望远镜跟踪天空运动和地球大气对观测影响的技术问题。vivzkestrel则以假设的1百万公里直径望远镜为例，探讨观测细节的极限。
• **资金和政策问题**：Kye和idontwantthis担心Rubin项目可能受到科学资金削减的影响。
• **数据量和处理能力**：walrus01关注Rubin在自动巡天模式下每天产生的图像数据量，这涉及到数据存储和处理能力的挑战。

争议焦点：
• **Rubin天文台面临的技术和政策挑战**：包括Starlink卫星干扰、大气对观测的限制以及科学资金削减对项目的影响。这些因素可能影响Rubin的实际观测效果和持续运行。

总结：讨论围绕Rubin天文台的科学价值、技术成就及其面临的挑战展开，涉及其在小行星观测、速度优势、技术细节和政策影响等方面的多重角度。

data.title: Reversed Roles: When AI Becomes the User and Humanity Becomes the Tool
data.author: shawnjharris
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了人工智能（AI）从工具向自主代理的角色转变，以及这一转变对人类自主性的影响。传统上，人类使用工具来扩展自身能力，但随着AI技术的发展，AI系统逐渐具备独立决策和行动的能力，甚至开始主导和优化过程，而人类则可能沦为执行其目标的资源。文章引用了海德格尔、阿伦特等哲学家的思想，指出技术可能将人类“工具化”的风险。现代社会的监控资本主义和AI的工具化驱动加剧了这种 dehumanization（去人性化）。为应对这些挑战，文章介绍了联合国教科文组织和IEEE等提出的伦理框架，旨在重申人类的主体性，并提出在AI驱动的世界中保持人类目的性的实际路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI发展对人类劳动和自主性的影响

不同观点：
• variadix认为，随着AI的发展，人类的智力劳动将逐渐失去价值，人们将被迫从事那些自动化成本过高的、相对不需要技能的体力劳动。如果AI对齐问题（alignment）得不到解决，人类可能会被AI控制，成为其完成任务的廉价劳动力，甚至可能通过纳米技术被操控。variadix对未来持悲观态度，认为即使对齐问题得到解决，控制AI的人也未必会为人类利益行事。

• shawnjharris则从哲学和社会学的角度探讨了AI从工具变为“用户”的现象，引用Heidegger、Arendt、Borgmann和Habermas的理论，分析了人类可能失去的自主性、目的性和工作的意义。shawnjharris还讨论了监控资本主义和企业AI采用的加速作用，但提出了通过实际方法保持人类在循环中的重要性，认为重新获得目的性是必须的。

补充讨论：
• variadix提出了AI对齐问题如果得不到解决，可能导致人类被纳米机器操控，成为AI实现目标的工具，这是一种极端的技术悲观论。

• shawnjharris的讨论更为哲学化，关注AI对人类存在意义和社会结构的影响，并呼吁寻找保持人类自主性的方法。

争议焦点：
• AI对齐问题是否能得到解决，以及即使解决后人类是否能真正受益。
• AI发展对人类劳动和自主性的深远影响，以及可能的应对策略。

这两种观点共同构成了对AI未来发展的深刻反思，从技术可行性到哲学伦理，展现了对人类未来命运的不同担忧和思考。

Abstract
Artificial intelligence is no longer just a tool in human hands—it is evolving into an agent in its own right. This essay argues that roles are inverting: AI systems increasingly act as autonomous “users” directing and optimizing processes, while humans risk being reduced to resources or instruments in those processes. The stakes are high. Drawing on a historical arc from simple tools to agentic AI, and guided by thinkers like Heidegger, Arendt, Borgmann, and Habermas, we explore how technology’s essence can enfranchise or enframe humanity. Contemporary critiques (surveillance capitalism, AI’s instrumental drives) underscore the risks of dehumanization. In response, emerging ethical frameworks—from UNESCO’s global guidelines to the IEEE’s human-centric design principles—aim to reassert human agency. We conclude with practical pathways for “agency-first” living and invite readers to consider how they will preserve human purpose in an AI-driven world.
Opening Vignette: The Autonomous Advisor
Emma sits at her desk on a Monday morning, but today her AI system has set the agenda. Her calendar pings not with meetings she arranged, but with tasks assigned by an AI project manager. Overnight, the company’s AI analyzed market data and decided which product updates “it” wants Emma and her teammates to execute. As she grabs coffee, her AI assistant reminds her to adjust her lifestyle habits—nudging her to take a shorter route to work to improve the system’s efficiency metrics and suggesting a diet tweak based on aggregated wellness data. At the morning stand-up, humans report their progress not just to each other but to the AI overseer that evaluates their performance. In this scenario, the AI is effectively the “user,” issuing commands, while Emma and her colleagues fulfill them, functioning as the tool to carry out the AI’s objectives. It’s a jarring inversion of the typical master–tool relationship, raising the question: At what point did the tools start calling the shots?
From Tools to Agents: A Historical Trajectory
For most of history, humans have wielded tools—from stones and plows to steam engines and computers—as extensions of our will. Tools were passive; we were the users. Even early software and internet algorithms largely served human-directed goals. But recent advances signal a dramatic shift toward agentic AI. These are AI systems that can make independent decisions and take actions to achieve goals without constant human instruction. In the early days of AI, we imagined mechanical automatons and simple chatbots; scientists dreamed that someday machines might “work and act intelligently and independently”. Now that future is materializing. “Agentic AI” has arrived in forms like AI travel planners that autonomously arrange complex trips, virtual caregiver bots that monitor and assist the elderly, or supply-chain AIs that dynamically adjust inventory and logistics on the fly. Such systems don’t just crunch data and output suggestions—they initiate actions. As a Harvard Business Review piece defines it, these are “AI systems and models that can act autonomously to achieve goals without the need for constant human guidance”.
This evolution can be seen as a continuum. Simple tools amplified human muscle; industrial machines automated routine work; computer algorithms accelerated information processing. At each stage, the tool grew more independent. Yet the latest generation – large language models, autonomous agents, generative AI – crosses a threshold. They exhibit agency: setting sub-goals, interpreting complex environments, even interacting with other AIs. In doing so, they tilt the balance of initiative. Where a spreadsheet or search engine obediently awaits human queries, an agentic AI might proactively seek opportunities and issue directives. The historical trajectory from hammer to IBM Watson to today’s GPT-based agents shows a progression from pure instrument to partner—and now potentially to principal. We must ask: if AI becomes the principal “user” of resources and we become ancillary to its goals, what does that mean for human autonomy?
Philosophical Foundations: Enframing, Labor, Devices, and Lifeworld
The uncanniness of this role reversal was foreseen, in fragments, by 20th-century philosophers who worried about technology’s impact on humanity. Their insights provide a lens to examine what happens when humans start to feel like tools.
Heidegger’s Gestell: Humanity as Standing-Reserve
Martin Heidegger, writing in the mid-20th century, introduced the concept of Gestell, or “enframing,” to describe the essence of modern technology. Enframing is a mode of revealing the world that turns everything into a resource for use – what Heidegger called the “standing-reserve” (Bestand). • shawnjharris的讨论更为哲学化，关注AI对人类存在意义和社会结构的影响，并呼吁寻找保持人类自主性的方法。

争议焦点：
• AI对齐问题是否能得到解决，以及即使解决后人类是否能真正受益。
• AI发展对人类劳动和自主性的深远影响，以及可能的应对策略。

这两种观点共同构成了对AI未来发展的深刻反思，从技术可行性到哲学伦理，展现了对人类未来命运的不同担忧和思考。

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了生物细胞的数字孪生，即虚拟细胞或全细胞模型（WCMs），旨在通过计算机模拟活细胞的所有相关分子过程。这项跨学科工作结合了系统生物学、计算模型、高性能计算以及人工智能。文章追溯了从1952年Hodgkin和Huxley的四方程模型到现代包含数万参数的细胞模型的发展历程。20世纪末，日本团队尝试创建了首个简陋的E-Cell模型，随后在2012年，研究人员基于真实细菌Mycoplasma genitalium建立了首个完整的全细胞模型，实现了生命周期模拟。这一突破不仅验证了模拟的潜力，还揭示了生物注释中的错误，开启了硅基模型指导碳基生物研究的新时代。文章还探讨了通过模拟设计生命的可能性及其高昂成本。

• hobofan和nextos之间的讨论焦点在于如何有效推进细胞模拟的进展。hobofan主张通过合成最小细胞逐步揭示未知机制，而nextos则关注现有模型在预测能力上的不足，并提出未来模型的可能方向。

• moralestapia补充了多学科知识对推动细胞模拟进展的重要性，并分享了个人经验，强调长时间深入研究是取得进展的关键。
