44331318.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
June 20, 2025
29 Minutes
This week at long last we come to the clash of men and horses as we finish our three-part (
I
,
II
, III) look at the iconic opening battle scene from the film
Gladiator
(2000).  Last time, we brought the sequence up through the infantry advance, observing that the tactics of the Roman arrow barrage and infantry assault weren’t very Roman at all and were poorly executed in either case.
This week, we’re closing out the battle with the final, confused melee as the infantry, barbarians and cavalry all come together in a swirling mess.  As we’re going to see, not only did Roman warfare seek to avoid such a swirling mess on the battlefield, so did the warfare of Germanic-speaking peoples like the Marcomanni and the Quadi – the ostensible enemies in this scene – who fought in spear-and-shield walls that relied on keeping formation every bit as much as the Romans.  Meanwhile Maximus, who is supposed to appear supremely capable, comes off as a deeply incompetent Roman commander who ought never have been trusted with command.
The result, as we’ve seen so far, is that while the Roman army in
Gladiator
is a lot of folks’ standard reference point for the Roman army, it doesn’t function very much like a Roman army.  Instead, its historical groundness is largely deceptive, getting just enough of the obvious things close enough to right for an audience to largely accept the things which are wrong.
But first, if you want to help support this project you can do so on
Patreon
! I don’t promise to use your money to buy myself more arms and armor, but I also don’t promise
not
to do that. And if you want updates whenever a new post appears, you can click below for email updates or follow me on
Twitter
and
Bluesky
and (less frequently) Mastodon (@bretdevereaux@historians.social) for updates when posts go live and my general musings; I have largely shifted over to Bluesky (I maintain some
de minimis
presence on Twitter), given that it has become a much better place for historical discussion than Twitter.
Email Address
Subscribe!
Whoopsiedoodles.
The Barbarians
But before we dive into the clash of infantry, I want to turn our focus briefly and look at bit more closely at the Marcomanni and Quadi in this scene,
because they are done even worse by it than the Romans, by some margin
, in how they are equipped, dressed and how they fight.
What we see of our ‘barbarians’  is all over the place, but mostly
conforms to the sort of ‘barbarian chic’ I have complained about in the past
: lots of leather and fur, dirty clothes and earth tones.  In equipment, we see few helmets, an absurd variety of shield shapes (most rectangular to some degree and curved) and a lot of axes (because barbarians love axes).  Their formation is likewise poor: they form a vaguely linear mass, but when the arrow barrage starts, we see men running around in every direction, with no particular order or effort to retain formation.  When they charge, there’s no effort to retain any kind of order, they simply rush forward in a rolling mass.
The one interesting quirk, of course, is that their leader speaks flawless 21st century
Bundesdeutsches Hochdeutsch
– an awkward and unfortunate equating of modern Germans with ancient Germanic-language speakers, as we noted last time – and they use the pre-battle murmur call from
Zulu
(1964). That murmur call was, so far as I know, entirely made up in 1964 and isn’t any less made up in 2000, but it is actually a neat film reference in that it encourages the viewer to think of how the white North-and-Central Europeans in this scene are the ones in the position of the “other” like the Zulu were in the 1800s, at the ‘business end’ of imperial exploitation. In that, it mirrors the earlier lines about who would “know when they are conquered.” Again, I am not entirely hostile to Ridley Scott and he’s at his best with these sorts of general themes, in the same way that
Kingdom of Heaven
(2005)
1
is mediocre as a history of the fall of the Kingdom of Jerusalem but
fantastic
as a study of how internal politics and ideologies impel states into foolish, counter-productive wars.
Our ‘German Leader,’ tossing the head of the Roman emissary.  They’ve given him a great big two-handed axe, but the prestige weapon in his culture in this period would have been a one-handed sword.  A proper Marcomannic or Quadi chieftain or king would also have worn a helmet and mail, and carried a shield, probably oval, and brightly painted.  A warrior like that, clad in gleaming metal armor with a bright, well-painted shield would cut an imposing figure on the battlefield.
But the rest of the depiction is pure nonsense.
What ought we see?
Instead of leathers and furs, in terms of dress, we ought to see the Marcomanni and Quadi wearing wool tunic and trousers, probably dyed in fairly bold primary and secondary colors.  Given the poor weather, they might wear cloaks (also wool), but generally people don’t wear cloak

data.title: Breaking WebAuthn, FIDO2, and Forging Passkeys
data.author: vmfunc
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了对WebAuthn、FIDO2和Passkeys安全机制的深入研究，展示了如何利用其潜在漏洞进行攻击。作者通过拆解硬件安全密钥和平台认证器，分析了CTAP2协议和WebAuthn API的工作机制，并开发了一个软件模拟器，通过USB-HID假冒FIDO2设备。作者还演示了如何伪造和重放Passkey签名，以在无需真实安全密钥的情况下实现自动登录。文章详细描述了捕获和解析真实WebAuthn注册过程中的通信数据，并探讨了防止密钥克隆的安全措施。最终，作者提供了一个跨平台命令行工具作为概念验证，展示了这种攻击的可行性和威胁模型，并提出了针对浏览器和依赖方（RP）的具体加固建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FIDO2和passkey实现中的安全性和验证问题，特别是关于认证声明验证和潜在的伪造风险。

不同观点：
• **[rlpb]**：认为这个问题并不是新发现。除非网站明确要求并验证认证声明，否则不良的FIDO2软件实现才会让用户处于风险之中。换句话说，如果网站不验证，用户选择使用不安全的实现是其自身责任。

• **[geoctl]**：指出大多数B2C甚至B2B网站在注册时并不会验证认证声明，这意味着他们无法确认公钥是否来自真实的安全设备（如TPM等），这可能导致安全隐患。同时提到FIDO MDS虽然能部分解决该问题，但可能误伤合法软件生成的passkey，尤其是TPM设备在处理认证时往往不完整，增加了复杂性。

• **[jiveturkey]**：对伪造和克隆问题表示困惑，认为如果用户已经拥有密钥材料，那么签名是基于自己的密钥生成的，而不是伪造。同时质疑文章是否过度解读了逆向工程工作，认为有些内容只是解码而非真正的逆向工程，且未明确展示任何凭证克隆的实际案例。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否存在严重的伪造风险，以及逆向工程工作的实际意义。
• **技术细节**：TPM设备在处理认证声明时的不完整性以及FIDO MDS作为解决方案的局限性。
• **实际应用中的问题**：许多网站在验证过程中缺乏对认证声明的检查，使得用户容易受到不良实现的影响。
• **关于逆向工程的争论**：部分讨论者认为文章对逆向工程的描述更像是简单的解码工作，而非真正的技术突破。

44329658.article_content:
Breaking WebAuthn, FIDO2, and Forging Passkeys
Fri Jun 20 2025
authored by
vmfunc
Introduction
Passwords are dying—slowly, awkwardly, and not without a fight.  Large parts of the internet are already nudging users toward "passkeys", the marketing-friendly name for FIDO2 credentials that live on your phone, security key, or TPM.
In theory passkeys solve phishing and credential-stuffing in one swoop.  In practice... they might introduce a shiny new attack surface:
A complex binary protocol (
CTAP2
) speaking over USB-HID, NFC and BLE.
JSON-ish CBOR blobs (
"COSE"
objects) glued together with bespoke signature schemes.
A browser API (
WebAuthn
) juggling credential IDs, transports, resident keys, UV / UP semantics and platform quirks.
Plenty of room for mistakes! Or for carefully crafted tooling that bends the spec in useful ways :3
Today, we will:
Tear apart a commercial hardware key and a "platform" authenticator to see what actually gets signed.
Build a software authenticator that impersonates a FIDO2 device over USB-HID. No kernel drivers, only usermode code.
Forge and replay passkey signatures to automate headless logins on sites that "require" WebAuthn.
Explore the security boundaries. What stops us from cloning credentials? How do Apple & Google lock down key material? Where do browser mitigations kick in?
By the end we'll have a working PoC: a cross-platform command-line tool that registers a fake passkey and logs you in without touching a real security key, and a clear understanding of which scenarios make this an interesting threat model!
Sound fun? Let's plug in a key and start sniffing packets.
Quick-Start Overview
Below is the 30-second tour of the entire project.  Treat it as a table of contents you can mentally pin while reading the deep-dives that follow.
Sniff
raw CTAP2 traffic with Wireshark and a tiny Python filter.
Decode
every CBOR/COSE field and locally verify Yubico's packed attestation.
Re-implement
the CTAP2 state-machine in pure Rust and exercise it in pipe-mode.
Inject
deterministic P-256/Ed25519 keys so signatures become reproducible.
Hijack
Chrome's hidden Virtual Authenticator via the DevTools Protocol.
Stress-test
our spoofed key against Google, Microsoft, GitHub & friends.
Harden
the ecosystem with concrete mitigations for browsers and RPs.
If you wish to follow along,
you can find the code and everything else
here
.
Capturing Real-World Traffic
Plugging the YubiKey in and hitting start immediately showered Wireshark with traffic—almost 200 frames before I could blink.  A quick scan of the text export (
yubi1.txt
) shows nothing but USB enumeration and CCID smart-card chatter.  The FIDO HID endpoints (
0x04 OUT
/
0x84 IN
) are alive, but every
URB_INTERRUPT
carries
zero
bytes.  No surprise: I haven't asked the browser to speak WebAuthn yet.
Endpoint: 0x84, Direction: IN
URB transfer type: URB_INTERRUPT (0x01)
Packet Data Length: 0
Lesson one: the authenticator stays silent until a site calls
navigator.credentials.create()
or
get()
.  Time to poke it.
Right after insertion: only device descriptors and smart-card traffic.
A quick glance at the
USB ID
lines confirms the stick really is a YubiKey,
idVendor 0x1050
,
idProduct 0x0407
matching Yubico's public list.  Handy reference:
YubiKey USB ID values
.
Tiny log-parser helper
Before recording the real ceremony I threw together a few lines of Python to sift the Wireshark TXT export for any 64-byte HID reports on those endpoints.  It spits raw hex one frame per line.
endpoint_re
=
re
.
compile
(
r"Endpoint:\s+0x(04|84)"
)
hex_re
=
re
.
compile
(
r"Leftover Capture Data:\s*([0-9A-Fa-f ]+)"
)
…
Running it on the first dump produces… nothing, confirming the absence of CTAP2 traffic.
The next step is obvious! trigger an actual WebAuthn registration while capturing, then feed the fresh TXT through the same script.
Capturing a WebAuthn registration ceremony.
Decoding the HID INIT handshake
The first two 64-byte frames look like this (hex trimmed):
ffffffff 86 0008 ed46b11ffcad30e6 ...
ffffffff 86 0011 ed46b11ffcad30e6 aa65678b 0205040305 ...
ffffffff
is the broadcast CID,
0x86
is the
INIT
command. The key echoes my 8-byte nonce and hands back an assigned channel ID (
aa65678b
) plus version/capability flags.  I then wrote a tiny helper to decode it:
$ python scripts/hid_init_decode.py
\
ffffffff860008ed46b11ffcad30e6
\
ffffffff860011ed46b11ffcad30e6aa65678b0205040305
INIT req → nonce ed46b11ffcad30e6
INIT resp → nonce
echo
matches: True assigned CID aa65678b
version
2
, capabilities 050403
With the private channel established, every subsequent packet starts with that CID.  The next command (
0x90
) carries the CTAP2
makeCredential
request body. Time to crack that CBOR.
Decoding & Verifying Attestation Data
This hexadecimal soup is useless until we map it back to WebAuthn's data structures.  We need to transform the captured frames into structured JSON, dissect the
makeCredential
request/response pair, and cryptographically prove the attesta

data.title: Mystery Powerful Radio Pulse Traced Back to NASA Satellite Dead Since 1967
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 在2024年6月13日，澳大利亚平方公里阵列探路者望远镜发现一个来自轨道的奇特无线电脉冲信号，最终追溯到已失效的NASA Relay 2卫星。这颗1964年发射的卫星在1965年停止运行，1967年后失去联系。科学家认为，信号可能是卫星积累的静电释放所致，类似于之前阿雷西博望远镜观察到的现象。另一种可能是微陨石撞击卫星产生等离子体云导致信号。虽然类似“僵尸卫星”复活的现象曾发生过，如2002年重新通信的AMSAT-OSCAR 7，但此次Relay 2的信号并非卫星复活，而是物理现象所致。研究这些事件有助于保护航天器和改善无线电观测。相关论文即将发表于《天体物理学杂志》。

44330391.article_content:
Impression of the Relay Satellite
Image Credit: public domain via
NH2501/Wikimedia Commons
DOWNLOAD PDF VERSION
The dead speak! Humanity has heard a mysterious signal, but the origin is not a broadcast from
Star Wars
’ Emperor Palpatine – it is from another seemingly defunct object. The NASA Relay 2 satellite, which worked for several years in the 1960s, appears to have sent a radio pulse back to Earth. Is the satellite back to life? Scientists think that something else might be going on.
On June 13, 2024, researchers at the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder spotted a peculiar emission in the sky. It was less than 30 nanoseconds, and analysis showed that it did not come from deep space but from orbit. The location of the signal suggested that the source was an old and defunct NASA satellite, which was certainly unexpected.
Relay 1 and Relay 2 were experimental communication satellites funded by NASA. Relay 1, launched in 1962, was the first satellite to broadcast television from the United States to Japan and Europe, with the first transmission being the Kennedy Assassination. Relay 2 launched in 1964, but it operated for just a short time, ceasing operations in September 1965. Still, its transponders were functional until 1967, when it was no longer heard from.
It could be argued until now, but Clancy James at Curtin University in Australia and colleagues do not believe this is the case. Just like beauty, this event is skin-deep. One possibility is that the satellite accumulated electrostatic charge, and it finally released a discharge. These ESDs (electrostatic discharges) have previously been seen by the
Arecibo telescope
, but on longer timescales.
There is also another possible explanation. A micrometeoroid, like the one that stranded astronauts a few years back after hitting the Soyuz spacecraft, can release a cloud of plasma at impact. That could cause such a signal. If it is an ESD, studying it could help researchers protect spacecraft from these events. And while you can’t stop a micrometeoroid, measuring these events can help remove them from radio wave observations.
While it is not the case this time, there are multiple instances of
zombie satellites
, satellites that came back to life after years of inactivity. Sometimes, these devices lose their orbit or can’t power themselves up, or get to a point where the ground can no longer contact them. Then it's usually clever people finding them, or occasionally, the satellites just say, “Guess what? I am back!”
Take, for example, Galaxy 15, a telecommunications satellite operated by Intelsat. It was launched in 2005, but in April 2010, it drifted out of its orbital slot and was lost. Well, the satellite knew where it was, and in December 2010, it
rebooted itself
. Intelsat was able to place it back into its original slot.
The record holder for zombie satellites is AMSAT-OSCAR 7, an amateur radio satellite launched in November 1974 and operated until 1981, when a battery failure ended the mission. Or so it seemed. On June 21, 2002, 21 years later, the satellite started communicating again.
A paper describing the new detection is accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal and is available to read on the
ArXiv
.
[H/T:
New Scientist
]

data.title: One Week Out, Some Brief Thoughts and Observations on WWDC 2025
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文是John Gruber对WWDC 2025的简短总结。他指出，苹果这次吸取了以往未兑现承诺的教训，专注于今年秋季能够交付的功能，且所有主要功能都已在开发者测试版中展示。苹果高管明确表示，计划在秋季发布会上展示的所有内容都会如期推出。Gruber认为，这种做法显示了苹果的信心和执行力。他还提到，基于年份的版本号虽然有些奇怪，但有助于统一各平台的发布周期，并确认每年主要版本的更新。此外，iPadOS的新窗口系统被认为比之前的分屏和滑动窗口更直观，尽管Stage Manager仍然保留，整体上iPadOS的多任务处理变得更加简单和明确。

By

One Week Out, Some Brief Thoughts and Observations on WWDC 2025
Thursday, 19 June 2025
“
This one a long time have I watched. All his life has he looked away — to the future, to the horizon. Never his mind on where he was. What he was doing. Adventure. Heh! Excitement. Heh! A Jedi craves not these things. You are reckless!
”
—Yoda,
The Empire Strikes Back
My biggest takeaway from WWDC 2025 is that Apple seemingly took some lessons to heart from
its unfulfilled promises
of a year ago. This year’s WWDC wasn’t merely focused on what Apple is confident it can ship in the next 12 months, but on what they can ship
this fall
. I might be overlooking a minor exception or two, but every major feature announced in
the WWDC 2025 keynote
was both demonstratable in product briefings,
and
is currently available in the developer beta seeds. I was also told, explicitly, by Apple executives, that Apple plans to ship everything shown last week in the fall.
That’s as it should be, and a strong return to form for the company. It takes confidence to promise only what you know you can ship, and it takes execution to ship what you’ve promised. If there’s more coming in the early months of 2026, announce those features when they’re ready. It’s proven very effective for Apple to spread the debut of new features across the entire calendar year, with many major features not appearing until the .3, .4, or even .5 OS releases. I think it will prove just as effective marketing-wise to spread the
announcement
of more features throughout the year as well.
Year-Based Version Numbers
There’s no question that it’s a little weird for every one of Apple’s platforms to have jumped to version 26. I mean, VisionOS skipped 23 version numbers. Presumably, when Apple next unveils a new OS (HomeOS?), it’s going to
start
at version 26, 27, or 28. But I’m already getting used to this, and I think the underlying logic laid out by Craig Federighi at the outset of the keynote is true: with Apple now up to six developer platforms (Mac, iPhone, iPad, Vision, TV, Watch), it had gotten hard to keep track of which version numbers corresponded to the same year. That matters not just for the convenience of knowing, in years to come, when specific versions of each OS were released, but it also matters because none of these platforms exist in isolation. They’re all parts of a cohesive whole, a cross-device “Apple OS 26” experience, as it were.
One thing I haven’t seen commented on, though, is that switching to year-based version numbers establishes as de facto policy something that has now been true for quite a few years, but which Apple has never officially acknowledged: that each of these platforms will get a major version release annually. 20 years ago the update schedule for Mac OS X was rather erratic:
Mac OS X 10.7 Lion
July 2011
Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard
August 2009
Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard
October 2007
Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger
April 2005
Mac OS X 10.3 Panther
October 2003
OS X 10.8 Mountain Lion (which began the odd four-year run where the Mac’s OS name didn’t contain “Mac”) arrived in July 2012, and thereafter a new major version has shipped in September, October, or November (MacOS 11 Big Sur, in 2020) every single year. This rigorous annual schedule is a hallmark of the Tim Cook era at Apple, and clearly reflects his personality (as the erratic/idiosyncratic schedule of the mid-2000s reflected Steve Jobs’s).
iPadOS Windowing
The pedant in me is mildly perturbed that the new windowing system unveiled for iPadOS 26 is largely being discussed under the term “multitasking”. It’s windowing. One way to understand the difference is that the original Mac OS (a.k.a. System 1) had windowing — windowing that looked and worked a lot like this — but no multitasking. The very early Mac could run just one app a time, but the running app could open multiple windows. But, whatever. It’s all good.
One thing I find interesting is that while
split screen and Slide Over
have been eliminated in the new system (
praise be
), Stage Manager is still a feature. Just plain windowing is as it should be: ad hoc. You make windows and move them around and resize them however you want. Stage Manager is fussier — it’s a more complex system for users who wish to organize their windows into something akin to projects or related tasks.
So, effectively, Apple, three years ago, jumped straight to a more complex, more fiddly option — Stage Manager — and only now has added the simpler, more obvious, not fiddly at all option (windowing). It’s been a weird journey, but I think iPadOS has finally arrived at a place where showing more than one app or document at a time on-screen is what it should have been all along: easy and obvious.

data.title: Defending the Internet: how Cloudflare blocked a monumental 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack
data.author: methuselah_in
data.article_summary: 2025年5月中旬，Cloudflare成功阻止了一次创纪录的7.3 Tbps DDoS攻击。此次攻击针对一家使用Cloudflare Magic Transit服务的托管服务商，攻击峰值达到每秒34,517个目标端口，主要由UDP洪水攻击（占99.996%）和其他多种反射与放大攻击构成。攻击在45秒内传输了37.4 TB数据，相当于约9,350部高清电影。Cloudflare的云端防护系统自动检测并缓解了此次攻击，保护了客户免受影响。文章还详细介绍了多种攻击类型及防御建议，如UDP、QOTD和Echo反射攻击的防护措施。

不同观点：
• kevmo314认为文章提供了关于QOTD协议（RFC865）的知识，将其视为互联网历史的一部分，表达了对这种技术 artifact 的欣赏。
• password4321对Cloudflare提出批评，认为Cloudflare一方面保护网站免受DDoS攻击，另一方面却可能与销售DDoS攻击的服务存在利益冲突，暗示这是“卖药的同时传播疾病”的行为。
• sparrish对具体DDoS攻击事件的背景感到好奇，特别是攻击目标、攻击的动机以及攻击的具体IP，显示出对DDoS攻击的技术细节和动机的兴趣。
• candiddevmike关注DDoS攻击背后的僵尸网络，特别是其平时如何运作、如何被“唤醒”以发起攻击，以及什么样的目标值得如此大规模的攻击，暗示出对僵尸网络管理和攻击目标选择的疑惑。

Defending the Internet: how Cloudflare blocked a monumental 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack
2025-06-19
Omer Yoachimik
9 min read
This post is also available in
FranÃ§ais
,
Nederlands
and
EspaÃ±ol
.
In mid-May 2025, Cloudflare blocked the largest DDoS attack ever recorded: a staggering 7.3 terabits per second (Tbps). This comes shortly after the publication of our
DDoS threat report for 2025 Q1
on April 27, 2025, where we highlighted attacks reaching 6.5 Tbps and 4.8 billion packets per second (pps). The 7.3 Tbps attack is 12% larger than our previous record and 1 Tbps greater than a recent attack reported by cyber security reporter Brian Krebs at
KrebsOnSecurity
.
New world record: 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack autonomously blocked by Cloudflare
The attack targeted a Cloudflare customer, a hosting provider, that uses
Magic Transit
to defend their IP network. Hosting providers and critical Internet infrastructure have increasingly become targets of DDoS attacks, as we reported in our
latest DDoS threat report
. Pictured below is an attack campaign from January and February 2025 that blasted over 13.5 million DDoS attacks against Cloudflareâs infrastructure and hosting providers protected by Cloudflare.
DDoS attack campaign target Cloudflare infrastructure and hosting providers protected by Cloudflare
Let's start with some stats, and then weâll dive into how our systems detected and mitigated this attack.
The 7.3 Tbps attack delivered 37.4 terabytes in 45 seconds
37.4 terabytes is not a staggering figure in todayâs scales, but blasting 37.4 terabytes in just 45 seconds is. Itâs the equivalent to flooding your network with over 9,350 full-length HD movies, or streaming 7,480 hours of high-definition video nonstop (thatâs nearly a year of back-to-back binge-watching) in just 45 seconds. If it were music, youâd be downloading about 9.35 million songs in under a minute, enough to keep a listener busy for 57 years straight. Think of snapping 12.5 million high-resolution photos on your smartphone and never running out of storageâeven if you took one shot every day, youâd be clicking away for 4,000 years â but in 45 seconds.Â
The record-breaking 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack delivered 37.4 TB in 45 seconds
The attack details
The attack carpet-bombed an average of 21,925 destination ports of a single IP address owned and used by our customer, with a peak of 34,517 destination ports per second. The attack also originated from a similar distribution of source ports.Â
Distribution of destination ports
Attack vectors
The 7.3 Tbps attack was a multivector DDoS attack. Around 99.996% of the attack traffic was categorized as UDP floods. However, the remaining 0.004%, which accounted for 1.3 GB of the attack traffic, were identified as QOTD reflection attacks, Echo reflection attack, NTP reflection attack, Mirai UDP flood attack, Portmap flood, and RIPv1 amplification attacks.
The attack vectors other than UDP floods
Breakdown of the attack vectors
Below are details about the various attack vectors seen in this attack, how organizations can avoid becoming a reflection and amplification participant, and recommendations on how to defend against these attacks whilst avoiding impact to legitimate traffic. Cloudflare's customers are protected against these attacks.
UDP DDoS attack
Type
: Flood
How it works:
A high volume of UDP packets is sent to random or specific ports on the target IP address(es). It may attempt to saturate the Internet link or overwhelm its in-line appliances with more packets than it can handle.
How to defend against the attack:
Deploy cloud-based volumetric DDoS protection, apply smart rate-limiting on UDP traffic, and drop unwanted UDP traffic altogether.
How to avoid unintended impact:
Aggressive filtering may disrupt legitimate UDP services such as VoIP, video conferencing, or online games. Apply thresholds carefully.
QOTD DDoS attack
Type:
Reflection + Amplification
How it works:
Abuses the Quote of the Day (QOTD) Protocol, which listens on UDP port 17 and responds with a short quote or message. Attackers send QOTD requests to exposed servers from a spoofed IP address, causing amplified responses to flood the victim.
How to prevent becoming a reflection / amplification element:
Disable the QOTD service and block UDP/17 on all servers and firewalls.
How to defend against the attack:
Block inbound UDP/17. Drop abnormal small-packet UDP request spikes.
How to avoid unintended impact:
QOTD is an obsolete diagnostic/debugging protocol and is not used by modern applications. Disabling it should not have any negative effect on legitimate services.
Echo DDoS attack
Type:
Reflection + Amplification
How it works:
Exploits the Echo protocol (UDP/TCP port 7), which replies with the same data it receives. Attackers spoof the victimâs IP address, causing devices to reflect the data back, amplifying the attack.
How to prevent becoming a reflection / amplification element:
Disable the Echo service on all devices. Block UDP/TCP

data.title: Apple Adds Energy and Battery Labels to iPhone and iPad Pages in EU
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 苹果公司在欧盟地区的iPhone和iPad页面上添加了能源效率标签，以遵守2025年6月20日生效的新规定。这些标签根据欧盟的测试参数对设备的能源效率进行评级，最高为A，最低为G。由于测试方法存在一些不明确之处，苹果保守地选择了较低评级，例如将原本符合A级的产品自愿降为B级。标签还包括电池寿命、可修复性、抗冲击性、防水防尘等级等信息。用户可以在苹果官网点击标签图标查看这些信息，同时还有一个详细的产品信息表供下载。欧盟数据库也提供相关能源标签信息。标签要求适用于奥地利、德国、法国等欧盟国家，以及挪威和瑞士。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple发布的白皮书及其引发的对欧洲监管过度和环保措施的讨论

不同观点：
• **[支持监管的立场（tosh）]**：tosh分享了Apple的白皮书链接，暗示对相关法规的支持，可能认为公司正在响应监管要求并提供透明信息。这种立场倾向于认为监管是必要且有帮助的。

• **[批评监管和产品质量的立场（everfrustrated）]**：everfrustrated批评了欧洲的环保法规和产品设计，认为这些法规导致了低效的家用电器，如洗碗机和洗衣机。该评论暗示，监管可能导致产品性能下降，从而影响用户体验。

• **[反对监管的立场（jiggawatts）]**：jiggawatts认为这类监管是官僚主义的过度干预，尽管表面上看似善意，但实际上会造成负面影响。他们指出，手机充电的电费成本非常低，制造商已经在优化能效以支持快速充电。强制性的文件工作和效率提升不会带来显著的经济或环境效益，反而浪费资源。评论还通过计算潜在的能源节约和合规成本，强调监管的成本可能超过其带来的好处。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于欧洲监管是否必要以及是否能带来实际的效益。jiggawatts特别质疑了法规的有效性，认为其带来的节约微不足道，而合规成本高昂。

• **论据和例子**：jiggawatts通过具体的数字计算（如电力成本、潜在节约、合规成本）来支持其反对立场。everfrustrated则通过列举其他据称因环保法规而降低性能的家用电器来加强其批评。

• **讨论的关系**：everfrustrated和jiggawatts的观点有相似之处，都对监管的效果持怀疑态度，但everfrustrated更关注产品性能，而jiggawatts则聚焦于经济和资源浪费的角度。

Apple Adds Energy and Battery Labels to iPhone and iPad Pages in EU
Friday June 20, 2025 10:08 am PDT
by
Joe Rossignol
To comply with a
new regulation
that
takes effect today
, Apple has added an energy efficiency label to its iPhone and iPad pages in EU countries. Apple is also required to start including a printed version of the label with the devices sold there.
The label grades a given iPhone or iPad model's energy efficiency from a high of A to a low of G, based on the EU's testing parameters. However, Apple said that certain aspects of the testing methods outlined by the European Commission are "ambiguous," so it chose to be conservative with its scores until testing is standardized.
In a
44-page document
detailing its testing methodology for the labels, Apple said its current iPhone models qualified for the highest energy efficiency grade of A, but the company voluntarily downgraded these scores to a B as a cautionary measure:
As an additional cautionary measure, Apple went one step further and downgraded some of its scores to factor in test method ambiguities and variance. For example, Energy Efficiency Index scores for iPhone models on the EU market in June 2025 all qualified for the highest "A" grade, but Apple chose to voluntarily derate scores to a "B" grade to minimize the probability that a third-party tester interpreting the regulation differently would achieve a lower grade. We also downgraded scores for the Repeated Free Fall Reliability Class for the same reason.
The label also provides details about a given iPhone or iPad model's battery life per full charge cycle, repairability grade, impact resistance, ingress protection rating for water and dust resistance, and how many full charge cycles the battery is rated for. Likewise, this information is based on Apple's interpretation of the EU's testing parameters.
On the web, the label can be viewed by clicking or tapping on the colorful little tag icon on various iPhone and iPad pages on Apple's localized websites for EU countries. It is shown on both Apple's main product marketing pages for all iPhone and iPad models that are currently sold in the EU, and on the purchase page for those devices.
The label is accompanied by a
product information sheet
(PDF) that provides a comprehensive overview of even more details, such as the device's battery capacity in mAh, screen scratch resistance based on the Mohs hardness scale, the minimum guaranteed timeframe for availability of security updates, and much more.
On the European Commission's website, there is a
database
that lets you view energy label information for smartphones and tablets sold in the EU.
More details about the label are available
on the European Commission's website
.
EU countries include Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden. The labels are also shown in Norway and Switzerland.

Take action
Around half of people are worried they’ll lose their job to AI.
1
And they’re right to be concerned: AI can now complete real-world coding tasks on GitHub, generate photorealistic video, drive a taxi more safely than humans, and do accurate medical diagnosis.
2
And it’s set to
continue to improve rapidly
.
But what’s less appreciated is that, while AI drives down the value of skills it
can
do, it drives up the value of skills it
can’t
— because they become the bottlenecks to further automation (for a while at least). As I’ll explain, ATMs actually
increased
employment of bank tellers — until online banking finished the job.
Your best strategy is to learn the skills that AI will make more valuable, trying to ride the wave one step ahead of automation. So what are those skills? Here’s a preview:
Skill
Why it's valuable
How to start
Deploying AI
AI makes people who can direct it more powerful. The messier parts that AI can't do become bottlenecks.
Use AI tools in your current job. Work at companies solving real problems with AI.
Personal effectiveness
Productivity, social skills, and rapid learning are useful in every job and compound the value of your other skills.
Use AI tutors to rapidly teach you new skills. Work with people who have these skills. Develop good habits.
Leadership skills
Management, strategy, and research taste are messy tasks AI struggles with, but AI gives leaders more influence than before.
Seek mentorship. Work at small, growing organisations, and seek small-scale management positions. Otherwise, start side projects. Study and apply best practice.
Communications and taste
Content creation gets automated, but discernment and trusting relationships with your audience become more valuable.
Build an authentic audience. Focus on personality-driven content. Work with people who have taste.
Getting things done in government
Citizens want real people making decisions, so knowing how to get things done in government remains crucial (even if many civil service positions disappear).
Follow standard routes into policy: staffer positions, internships, fellowships, government positions, and working with successful operators.
Complex physical skills
Robotics lags behind knowledge work, especially for specialist work in unpredictable environments.
Seek apprenticeships in growing fields (e.g. datacentre construction), or just get an entry-level job.
In contrast, the future for these skills seems a lot more uncertain:
Coding, applied math, and STEM
Routine white collar skills such as recall and application of established knowledge, routine writing, admin, and translation
Visual creation such as animation.
More routine physical skills such as driving
It’s hard to say what effect this will have on the job market overall, or how quickly it will unfold, but it seems likely that relatively entry-level white collar jobs such as in law, finance, tech, government, healthcare, and professional services will struggle, in favour of an expanded class of leaders overseeing AI agents, and with increasing wages. Small teams and individuals will have more leverage than before. Retail, manual, and physical presence jobs (e.g. police, teacher, surgeon, construction worker) in the bottom half of incomes will be relatively unaffected (incomes roughly keeping pace with GDP) at least until robotics catches up. On average, wages initially rise, but could eventually come under pressure.

data.title: 16B passwords from Apple, Facebook, Google and more leaked
data.author: rakibtg
data.article_summary: 文章报道了有史以来最大的数据泄露事件，涉及160亿个密码，包括Apple、Facebook、Google等账户以及政府服务。这次泄露的登录凭证可能被用于钓鱼攻击和账户接管。尽管数据短暂暴露，研究人员仍警告用户立即更改密码，并建议使用密码管理工具以提高安全性。FBI也提醒公众警惕可疑链接。此次泄露涉及多个信息窃取者，但具体受影响人数尚不明确。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在数据存储或传输时，应选择使用明文（plaintext）还是哈希值（hashes）

不同观点：
• 支持使用哈希值的观点：
  - 哈希值可以有效保护数据隐私，因为原始数据无法直接从哈希值中推导出来。
  - 哈希值在验证数据完整性方面非常有用，可以用来检测数据是否被篡改。
  - 举例：密码存储中常用哈希值来避免直接保存明文密码，防止泄露。

• 支持使用明文的观点：
  - 明文数据在某些场景下更容易理解和使用，特别是在需要直接读取和处理数据的场合。
  - 明文传输或存储在某些简单应用中可能更加高效，不需要额外的计算资源来生成和验证哈希。
  - 举例：在非敏感信息的传输中，使用明文可能更加便捷且没有安全顾虑。

• 对两种方法的折中观点：
  - 可以在不同场景下结合使用明文和哈希值，例如在需要保护隐私和验证完整性时使用哈希，而在需要直接访问数据时使用明文。
  - 建议在安全要求高的系统中使用哈希值，而在开发、测试或低风险环境下使用明文以提高效率。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于数据的安全性与可访问性、计算成本之间的平衡。
- 另一个值得注意的点是，使用哈希值虽然提升了安全性，但仍需防范哈希碰撞和彩虹表攻击等风险。
- 实际应用中，选择还可能受到法规、合规要求以及具体业务需求的影响。

Your support helps us to tell the story

Support Now
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.
At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
Your support makes all the difference.
Read more
Sixteen billion passwords to
Apple
,
Facebook
,
Google
, and other
social media accounts,
as well as government services, were leaked in what researchers are calling the largest data breach ever, according to reports.
The leak exposed 16 billion login credentials and passwords, prompting both Google to tell billions of users to change their passwords and the FBI to warn Americans against opening suspicious links in SMS messages, according to a report published Thursday in
Forbes.
Researchers at
Cybernews
, who have been investigating the leak, found “30 exposed datasets containing from tens of millions to over 3.5 billion records each.”
All but one of these datasets have not been previously reported as being exposed, so the data impacted is all considered new.
“This is not just a leak – it’s a blueprint for mass exploitation,” the researchers said. And they are right. These credentials are ground zero for phishing attacks and account takeover. “These aren’t just old breaches being recycled,” they warned, “this is fresh, weaponizable intelligence at scale.”
Sixteen billion passwords to Apple, Facebook, Google and other accounts were leaked in what researchers have called the largest data breach ever.
(
Alamy/PA
)
Recommended
Chinese hackers and user lapses turn smartphones into a 'mobile security crisis'
Hackers say they wiped out $90 million from Iran cryptocurrency exchange
Co-op offering 25% discount after cyber attack - here’s how to claim yours
Most of that intelligence was in the format of a URL, followed by logins and passwords. That information then allowed access to “pretty much any online service imaginable, from Apple, Facebook, and Google, to GitHub, Telegram, and various government services.”
While worrisome, the researchers found that the datasets were exposed very briefly – with enough time for them to be discovered, but not long enough for researchers to figure out who was controlling the data.
Researchers have determined the leak is the work of multiple infostealers, but it’s impossible to tell how many people or accounts were exposed, according to Cybernews.
The experts urge people to invest in password management solutions, not share their passwords and to stay alert in the event their passwords are compromised.

data.author: nill0
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Nadir Hajouji和Steve Trettel的一个项目，旨在可视化椭圆曲线（elliptic curves）。目前，该项目的网页正在建设中，邀请访问者耐心等待。文章还提到了一些相关的学术论文和精美的椭圆曲线图示。该项目旨在通过艺术形式展示数学概念，将抽象的椭圆曲线形象化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对椭圆曲线和零知识证明（zk proofs）可视化的不同观点和讨论，包括其美学价值、实用性、技术细节以及可能的应用场景。

不同观点：
• [欣赏与赞美]  
  - **cosmodev**: 作为长期从事椭圆曲线和零知识证明工作的人，认为这些可视化非常棒，视其为“极客艺术”。
  - **tempodox**: 称赞可视化让数学对象看起来像物理实体，甚至可以3D打印。
  - **ykonstant**: 原本预期会失望，但发现可视化不仅美观而且实用，尤其几何特性保留得很好，并推荐了相关论文。
  - **aanet**: 简单表达了对可视化作品的喜爱，认为非常漂亮。
  - **bedit**: 认为将抽象数学转化为视觉艺术很有趣，期待进一步的发展。
  - **gloosx**: 联想到自然界中的椭圆曲线，比如花朵，认为这些图像很吸引人。
  - **knottedoak**: 认为这些可视化对理解模性定理和费马大定理有很大帮助。

• [艺术与商业联想]  
  - **matcha-video**: 提到区块链上的程序化艺术，并引用了Tyler Hobbs的作品作为例子。
  - **felineflock**: 开玩笑地说想把图像印在T恤上，但担心被误认为外星甜甜圈店的品牌。
  - **broken_broken_**: 表示想买印有这些图像的T恤。

• [技术疑问与讨论]  
  - **charlieyu1**: 提出关于有限域上的椭圆曲线可视化的疑问，质疑其离散性如何呈现。
  - **larodi**: 提到与其他数学可视化工具（如Structure Synth和Context Free Art）的潜在联系，探讨了语法形式主义和椭圆曲线之间的数学联系。
  - **loxias**: 询问这些图像是否是用Blender渲染的，表现出对具体实现方法的好奇。
  - **Datagenerator**: 请求分享源代码，以便能够重现这些美丽的图像。

• [个人联想与感受]  
  - **HappMacDonald**: 联想到拓扑学中的球面反演过程，认为这些图像看起来像是该过程的中途状态。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：尽管评论整体积极，但**charlieyu1**对有限域上的椭圆曲线可视化的技术细节提出了疑问，这是评论中唯一对技术实现表示困惑的地方。
- 艺术与实用性：评论中不少人既赞赏了这些可视化的美学价值（如cosmodev、aanet），也有人强调了其实用性（如ykonstant、knottedoak）。
- 技术实现：多位评论者对可视化的具体实现方式（如3D打印、Blender渲染）表现出兴趣，并进行了相关讨论（tempodox、loxias、larodi）。

data.title: Getting Started Strudel
data.author: rcarmo
data.article_summary: Strudel是一个通过代码创作音乐的工具，是Tidal Cycles模式语言的JavaScript版本。无需JavaScript或Tidal Cycles基础即可使用。Strudel可用于实时编码音乐、算法作曲、教学以及集成到现有音乐设备中。它提供了一个交互式教程和REPL环境来帮助用户入门。用户可以通过代码控制样本、节奏和声音效果，创造丰富的音乐作品。文章还提供了代码示例和视频展示，帮助用户了解Strudel的潜力。学习Strudel的最佳起点是参与其工作坊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Strudel音乐工具的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• **积极评价与推荐**：
   - **milchek**：对Strudel的循环概念和音符数字表示方式印象深刻，认为这些功能使得旋律创作和即兴演奏变得有趣。同时提到Euclidean patterns的随机化支持，并推荐了Switch Angel的视频演示。
   - **jan_Inkepa**：赞赏编辑器在播放歌曲时高亮显示文件活跃部分的功能。
   - **dzink**：认为Strudel是一个低门槛且有趣的工具，既能创作音乐又能保存音乐创意，还能帮助人们轻松入门编程。

• **功能赞赏但文档批评**：
   - **henrebotha**：认为Strudel的流畅API和"display-oriented REPL"非常酷，但指出文档不足，API参考资料不全，功能发现性差，解释不权威。
   - **pwatsonwailes**：目前在使用Strudel的Superdough和transpiler部分，认为功能强大但文档不足。

• **其他体验与趣闻**：
   - **jarmitage**：分享了自己和Strudel合作发布的remix链接。
   - **whywhywhywhy**：认为Strudel的可视化反馈部分是一个很好的演示。
   - **joeatwork**：即使对用Strudel创作音乐不感兴趣，也推荐访问其网站以欣赏展示的多样音乐作品。
   - **JonnyReads**：回忆起在maker会议上接触到Algorave和现场编码音乐的经历，认为这是一个非常有趣的小众领域。
   - **crabmusket**：分享了大学时使用Tidal和Supercollider的经历，虽然技术不佳但乐趣十足。

• **技术迁移讨论**：
   - **Eduard**：提到Strudel从Github迁移到Codeberg，询问其他用户关于代码托管平台迁移的经验和建议。

• **幽默与轻松评论**：
   - **hermitcrab**：以幽默方式表示自己误以为是寻找苹果 strudel 的食谱。
   - **skeptrune**：认为编辑器是最酷的部分，使得工作展示变得容易且有趣。
   - **ItCouldBeWorse**：开玩笑地希望有一个LLM（语言模型）能够将歌唱和beatbox转换为Strudel代码。

补充讨论：
• **技术支持与使用提示**：
   - **thih9**：提醒iOS用户如果听不到示例声音，需要关闭静音模式。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在Strudel工具的文档不足问题上，虽然功能强大但文档和API参考资料的缺乏影响了用户体验。

44287248.article_content:
Welcome
Welcome to the Strudel documentation pages!
Youâve come to the right place if you want to learn how to make music with code.
What is Strudel?
With Strudel, you can expressively write dynamic music pieces.
It is an official port of the
Tidal Cycles
pattern language to JavaScript.
You donât need to know JavaScript or Tidal Cycles to make music with Strudel.
This interactive tutorial will guide you through the basics of Strudel.
The best place to actually make music with Strudel is the
Strudel REPL
What can you do with Strudel?
live code music: make music with code in real time
algorithmic composition: compose music using tidalâs unique approach to pattern manipulation
teaching: focussing on a low barrier of entry, Strudel is a good fit for teaching music and code at the same time.
integrate into your existing music setup: either via MIDI or OSC, you can use Strudel as a really flexible sequencer
Examples
Here are some examples of how strudel can sound:
// "coastline" @by eddyflux
// @version 1.0
samples('github:eddyflux/crate')
setcps(.75)
let chords = chord("<Bbm9 Fm9>/4").dict('ireal')
stack(
stack( // DRUMS
s("bd").struct("<[x*<1 2> [~@3 x]] x>"),
s("~ [rim, sd:<2 3>]").room("<0 .2>"),
n("[0 <1 3>]*<2!3 4>").s("hh"),
s("rd:<1!3 2>*2").mask("<0 0 1 1>/16").gain(.5)
).bank('crate')
.mask("<[0 1] 1 1 1>/16".early(.5))
, // CHORDS
chords.offset(-1).voicing().s("gm_epiano1:1")
.phaser(4).room(.5)
, // MELODY
n("<0!3 1*2>").set(chords).mode("root:g2")
.voicing().s("gm_acoustic_bass"),
chords.n("[0 <4 3 <2 5>>*2](<3 5>,8)")
.anchor("D5").voicing()
.segment(4).clip(rand.range(.4,.8))
.room(.75).shape(.3).delay(.25)
.fm(sine.range(3,8).slow(8))
.lpf(sine.range(500,1000).slow(8)).lpq(5)
.rarely(ply("2")).chunk(4, fast(2))
.gain(perlin.range(.6, .9))
.mask("<0 1 1 0>/16")
)
.late("[0 .01]*4").late("[0 .01]*2").size(4)
These examples cannot fully encompass the variety of things you can do, so
check out the showcase
for some videos of how people use Strudel.
Getting Started
The best way to start learning Strudel is the workshop.
If youâre ready to dive in, letâs start with your
first sounds

data.title: Ask HN: What do you think about app native vs. portable look-and-feel?
data.author: ttd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的用户界面（UI）在跨平台和原生应用开发中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• **pellenys** 认为原生UI的使用带来了更好的一致性和可用性。他指出，原生UI基于多年经验形成的标准，比如Windows应用中的tab顺序和取消按钮映射到escape键等惯例。虽然跨平台UI也能用且美观，但缺乏原生UI的那种统一性，现在的Electron应用（如Slack、Spotify、VSCode）看起来和用起来都很不一样，这让用户在使用不熟悉的应用时感到不便。不过，他也承认跨平台UI大大节省了开发工作量，而多数人可能并不像他这么在意这些细节。

• **not_your_vase** 强调效率和性能，认为平台特定的原生工具包在性能上几乎总是胜过跨平台UI。他反感看到大量的内存和CPU资源被浪费在简单的界面显示上，比如一个跑马灯效果也要消耗大量资源。

• **saluki** 认为跨平台UI（如React Native）在视觉和感觉上已经表现得很专业，尽管他仍然认为原生UI更好，但也能接受跨平台UI的表现。

• **brudgers** 持实用主义观点，认为只要应用有用，用户不会在意是否是原生UI。如果应用没用，即使使用原生UI也无济于事。他指出，开发者可能对这个问题有强烈意见，但这些意见只在特定情况下（如工作面试）重要。应用的质量问题往往出在其他更难解决的地方，而纠结于是否使用原生UI只会增加开发复杂性，不如专注于让应用“能用”就好。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：原生UI和跨平台UI在可用性、一致性、性能和开发效率上的取舍。pellenys和not_your_vase更关注原生UI的传统优势，而saluki和brudgers则更能接受跨平台UI的实用性和现代发展趋势。
- **性能问题**：not_your_vase特别提到了性能问题，认为跨平台UI往往在性能上不如原生UI，造成资源浪费。
- **开发效率**：brudgers和pellenys都提到跨平台UI在开发效率上的优势，认为这是其被广泛采用的主要原因之一。

主要讨论点：不同类型的用户界面（UI）在跨平台和原生应用开发中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• **pellenys** 认为原生UI的使用带来了更好的一致性和可用性。他指出，原生UI基于多年经验形成的标准，比如Windows应用中的tab顺序和取消按钮映射到escape键等惯例。虽然跨平台UI也能用且美观，但缺乏原生UI的那种统一性，现在的Electron应用（如Slack、Spotify、VSCode）看起来和用起来都很不一样，这让用户在使用不熟悉的应用时感到不便。不过，他也承认跨平台UI大大节省了开发工作量，而多数人可能并不像他这么在意这些细节。

• **not_your_vase** 强调效率和性能，认为平台特定的原生工具包在性能上几乎总是胜过跨平台UI。他反感看到大量的内存和CPU资源被浪费在简单的界面显示上，比如一个跑马灯效果也要消耗大量资源。

• **saluki** 认为跨平台UI（如React Native）在视觉和感觉上已经表现得很专业，尽管他仍然认为原生UI更好，但也能接受跨平台UI的表现。

• **brudgers** 持实用主义观点，认为只要应用有用，用户不会在意是否是原生UI。如果应用没用，即使使用原生UI也无济于事。他指出，开发者可能对这个问题有强烈意见，但这些意见只在特定情况下（如工作面试）重要。应用的质量问题往往出在其他更难解决的地方，而纠结于是否使用原生UI只会增加开发复杂性，不如专注于让应用“能用”就好。

- **争议焦点**：原生UI和跨平台UI在可用性、一致性、性能和开发效率上的取舍。pellenys和not_your_vase更关注原生UI的传统优势，而saluki和brudgers则更能接受跨平台UI的实用性和现代发展趋势。
- **性能问题**：not_your_vase特别提到了性能问题，认为跨平台UI往往在性能上不如原生UI，造成资源浪费。
- **开发效率**：brudgers和pellenys都提到跨平台UI在开发效率上的优势，认为这是其被广泛采用的主要原因之一。

data.title: Posit floating point numbers: thin triangles and other tricks (2019)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过比较两种32位数字格式——IEEE binary32（即单精度浮点数）和posits（es=2），展示了它们在计算薄三角形面积时的表现差异。作者使用Heron公式计算三角形面积，并展示了精确值、posits计算结果和IEEE计算结果。结果显示，posits在精度上优于IEEE格式，尤其在处理细微差异时更为准确。文章还讨论了两种格式的历史背景和设计选择，指出IEEE格式在处理大数时精度不足，而posits则能在更大范围内保持较高精度。文章通过几个数值示例和幽默叙述，强调了posits在某些计算中的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Posits与IEEE浮点数(FP)的比较及其在不同应用场景中的优劣

不同观点：
• dnautics（Posits的创建者之一）：
  - 认为Posits不适用于科学计算，因为误差传播问题难以解决。
  - Posits更适合机器学习(ML)中的低位表示，误差传播在此不重要。
  - 提到Facebook对Posits的修改（对数尾数）以及硬件实现的困难。
  - 强调Posits在特定应用（如AI）中的潜力。

• burnt-resistor：
  - 分享了一个类似IEEE格式的速查表，提供了对不同格式的测试结果。

• mserdarsanli：
  - 开发了一个交互工具展示Posits，认为Posits在某些情况下比IEEE浮点数有更好的精度表现，但也有权衡。

• adrian_b：
  - 认为Posits在某些示例中表现出的高精度具有误导性，因为其误差分布不均匀。
  - 指出Posits在靠近零的区间精度高，但在远离零的区间误差大。
  - 认为Posits在科学计算中不实用，因为难以预测和控制误差，且需要硬件支持才能实现最佳性能。

• antiquark：
  - 提到Posits与Unum类型III相关，提供了背景信息。

• phkahler：
  - 对Posits的兴趣不在精度，而在其没有符号零和NaN，认为操作结果不应是非数字。

• im3w1l：
  - 提出纯指数格式的可能性，认为这种格式可以避免一些特殊情况，如零和NaN的处理。

• andrepd：
  - 对讨论表示高度兴趣，认为帖子提供了深刻的见解。

补充讨论：
- Posits的误差传播和分布问题是一个争议焦点，特别是在科学计算和复杂计算中。
- 不同应用场景（如AI与科学计算）对数值表示格式有不同需求，Posits在特定应用中可能有优势。
- 硬件实现的困难和现有GPU管线的兼容性是Posits推广的一个实际障碍。
- 对IEEE浮点数的替代方案有多种提议，每种方案在不同应用中有其优缺点。

February
6th,
2019
WARNING:
Some numerical analysis and mathematics will be mentioned in passing. Also the number systems will not be treated like black-boxes. Risk of physical injury, however, is negligible.
I like magic tricks. Watching the performer do the show and attempting to catch the “slight-of-hand” that makes the impossible seem possible. It’s fun and makes me believe in magic for a few moments. So I’m going to give a shot at doing some floating point magic tricks.
Throughout my performance I’ll use two 32-bit formats:  IEEE
binary32
(aka singles or
float
in a number of languages) and
posits
(with es=2).
NARRATOR:
For general purpose computations 32-bit is about as small as we can push, otherwise bit size choice doesn’t matter.  Gustafson uses
es=3
to cover the range of
binary32
but suggests that
es=2
is a better and it look like that’s the value they’re running with for the specification.  The choice doesn’t matter in the slightest for this discussion.
Originally this was going to be one big post but I’ve decided to break in in parts. Source code will be provided in a later version (for reasons). There are so many intertwined issues that it’s almost impossible to provide some nice linear presentation.
Goldberg’s long thin triangle
performance LIVE on stage
NARRATOR:
Kahan presented this problem in or prior to 1986 and the Goldberg paper (from 1991) was inspired from attended a conference by Kahan.
We are going totally compute the area $A$ of a thin triangle using the classic form of
Heron’s equation
. Life’s way too short to think about computation!
\[\begin{align*}
s & = \frac{a+b+c}{2} \\
A & = \sqrt{s\left(s-a\right)\left(s-b\right)\left(s-c\right)}
\end{align*}\]
With a wave of my hand I declare the lengths to be:
\[\begin{align*}
a & = 7 \\
b & = c= \frac{1}{2}\left(a+3~\text{ulp}\left(a\right)\right)
\end{align*}\]
and let’s pull out of my magic computationalizing box the exact, the
super-mojo-exponent
and
tapering-precision-just-exactly-where-you-need-it
posits and poor old
binary32
results (wrong digits in red):
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 7.831550 \times 10^{-3} \\
\text{posit} & = 7.831550 \times 10^{-3} \\
\text{IEEE}  & = \color{red}{9.043097} \times 10^{-3}
\end{align*}\]
Booyah!
In your face ya old retired, don’t publish papers anymore, stuck in the 80s people! Posits are, like, exact and you got ZERO digits correct!
NARRATOR:
Attempting a detailed comparison between two formats which are both base-2 in base-10 is misleading.
Ahhh…okay.  Let’s look again:
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 1000000001001111111001110 \times 2^{-31} \\
\text{posit} & = 100000000100111111100111\color{red}{1} \times 2^{-31} \\
\text{IEEE}  & = 100\color{red}{1010000101001011111110} \times 2^{-31}
\end{align*}\]
CAT-A-STROPIC!
only
3
out of 24 binary digits correct vs. 23!
NARRATOR:
Yes. I see what you did there. Very clever, but then again Gustafson titled his mathematica example
“Thin triangle area with posits: an unfair fight”
I’m going to do this trick again, but first I want to tell a story. Way back in 1985..raise your hand if you were even born yet. Yeah? A couple of people. Ok, well, back in the day integer adders were super cheap and integer multiplier super expensive SO the IEEE committee was all like
“Okay..let’s make the exponent part bigger (since that needs adders) and the fractional bits part smaller(that the multipliers)!”
.  I suppose that was fine then, but man-oh-man have things changed. Like we just saw…singles only have 24 bit of precision (AT MOST!) and totally fail at a simple computation.  But at the same time can represent really stupid big numbers! Get this: the largest finite number a single can represent is almost $2^{128}$. I think mathematicians call numbers like this googleperplexing…probably because even searching the web won’t help you understand them. See what I mean. Way too big.  That’s why I’m using posits with es=2. With that we still represent numbers up to $ {2^{120}} $ AND have more precision. Maybe a better choice would be to use es=3..that would slightly hurt our precision, but we’d be able to drop-in-replace IEEE doubles with 32-bit posits (how dope is that?)…but I’m going to stick with my choice for now.
NARRATOR:
Knuth once said:
“The idea that people knew a thing or two in the ’70s is strange to a lot of young programmers.”
Let’s do the same thing again, but this time with a reasonably big, but not googleperplexing, number: $a=3670016$.
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 100000000100111111100111 \times 2^{8}              & \approx 2.1527203 \times 10^{9} \\
\text{posit} & = \color{red}{0}  \\
\text{IEEE}  & = 100\color{red}{101000010100101111111} \times 2^{8} & \approx 2.4857475 \times 10^{9}
\end{align*}\]

Fun fact: $2^{120}$ = 1329227995784915872903807060280344576
Yeah, yeah okay…millions is silly, let’s use a more realistic number: $a=917504$

data.title: Wiki Radio: The thrilling sound of random Wikipedia
data.author: if-curious
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Wiki Radio的趣味项目，用户可以随机收听上传至Wikimedia的各种声音，包括政治演讲、鸟叫声以及音乐等，大多数内容健康，但偶尔可能出现不合适的声音。用户还可以选择"Revolution 9 Mode"来收听较短的声音片段。项目末尾鼓励用户向维基百科捐款，并注明了相关素材的来源和版权信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某多媒体项目（可能是音频集合或随机音频体验）的评价和反馈

不同观点：
• [mycatisblack] 认为该项目中的日语歌曲由于文字竖排排列，导致无法识别艺术家，体验上存在不便。
• [RheingoldRiver] 对项目中"Revolution 9"模式下重复播放"Number 9"的人工声音表示不满，认为其令人烦躁，但总体上对项目的其他音频内容（如动物声音、音乐、不同语言的演讲等）表示赞赏，只有在遇到不愉快的声音时才会跳过。
• [saretup] 也提到静态噪音在音频之间的出现令人不快，认为这种设计很快会让人厌烦。
• [ghastmaster] 分享了个人体验，表示在随机跳到第三个音频时非常喜欢，并提供了相关YouTube链接，显示了对项目的积极态度，同时表达了对项目带来意外发现的惊喜。
• [guerrilla] 对项目给予高度评价，认为其带来了类似于StumbleUpon的体验，并引发了对人类创造力的一些积极思考。
• [Tokkemon] 只引用了"Number 9"的重复声音，可能是在呼应[RheingoldRiver]的评论，暗示对这一部分的不满。
• [komali2] 对项目表示赞赏，甚至有些嫉妒这个创意，暗示项目非常有吸引力。
• [laszlojamf] 对项目表示喜爱，但提出该项目类似于"vibe coding"革命的产物，认为LLMs（大型语言模型）帮助实现了这类小创意，暗示技术进步对创意实现的推动作用。
• [mbil] 从标题预期项目会是类似于谈话说 radio的风格（如NotebookLM风格）的随机维基页面讨论，显示出对项目内容的不同预期和理解。

补充讨论：
• 用户对项目中某些设计（如"Number 9"的重复声音和静态噪音）存在争议，部分用户认为这些元素令人烦躁。
• 项目带来的意外发现和随机性被一些用户（如[ghastmaster]和[laszlojamf]）视为积极元素，增加了探索的乐趣。
• 技术（如LLMs）在创意项目实现中的作用也被提及，显示出对技术进步如何影响创意表达的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 项目中重复声音和静态噪音的设计是否合适，部分用户认为其令人烦躁，而其他用户则可能因为整体体验的趣味性而忽略了这些不足。

data.author: ReadCarlBarks

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款名为Harper的语法检查工具，与Grammarly的对比，以及是否应该使用大语言模型（LLM）进行语言校正。

不同观点：
• **反对使用LLM的观点**：[pram]认为不使用LLM是一个优点，指出Grammarly在引入AI功能后变得 inconsistent，尤其是标点符号的建议反复无常。
• **支持使用LLM的观点**：[icapybara]质疑为何不使用LLM进行语言学习，认为LLM在处理英语错误方面非常可靠，并提到ChatGPT很少犯英语错误。
• **对工具规则基础的质疑**：[demarq]通过一个复杂的错误句子（"Me and Jennifer went to have seen the ducks cousin."）来测试Harper，指出其需要大量规则贡献才能达到Grammarly的水平。[cAtte_]进一步批评了手动编码语法规则的不足，认为在LLM时代，手动编码的校正能力有限，无法处理复杂的自然语言。
• **对LLM与传统工具的比较**：[IceWreck]认为自从LLM出现后，就不再使用Grammarly，即使是小型的本地LLM也能很好地改写文本和修正语法错误。

补充讨论：
• **功能改进建议**：[behnamoh]希望增加键盘快捷键和延迟检查功能，并建议引入导入/导出校正规则的选项，以提升使用体验，特别是对Vim用户。[orliesaurus]则指出该工具目前存在一些bug，但认为这是一个很好的开始。
• **对Automattic产品的不信任**：[healsdata]对Automattic的产品持怀疑态度，担心如果产品成功，可能会因盈利目的而被破坏。
• **工具的技术实现**：[JPLeRouzic]提供了工具的开源代码链接，方便用户查看技术细节。[sharkjacobs]进一步分析了Harper的规则基础，指出其依赖硬编码规则，并提供了具体示例和文档链接。

争议焦点：
• 是否应在语法检查工具中使用LLM，支持者认为LLM能更智能地处理语言，反对者则担心其一致性和可靠性问题。

data.title: AMD's Freshly-Baked MI350: An Interview with the Chief Architect
data.author: pella
data.article_summary: AMD在2025年AI大会上发布了MI350系列加速器，首席架构师Alan Smith接受了采访。MI350基于GFX9（Vega架构）优化，专注于高性能计算和AI应用。尽管GCN架构具有独立的L1缓存和本地数据存储（LDS），AMD在MI350中增加了LDS容量至160KB，并提升带宽以支持Tensor Core。MI350引入了微缩数据格式如FP8、FP6和FP4，其中FP6的处理速度与FP4相同，以提升AI训练和推理性能。此外，AMD选择不支持硬件加速的TF32，认为BF16能提供更高吞吐量，适合多数模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD Instinct MI350的硬件性能、市场应用及其与竞争对手（如Nvidia）的比较。

不同观点：
• Pella的观点：Pella解释了MI350在FP6数据路径上的设计选择，强调其在推理（inferencing）和训练（training）方面的潜力。为了确保FP6性能领先，AMD在硬件设计上增加了资源，使其在功耗和面积效率上具有优势。这个观点侧重于技术细节和设计决策。

• Latchkey的观点：Latchkey对MI350及其前代产品MI300x表现出期待，并表示计划部署MI355。这反映了对AMD产品的积极期待和实际使用体验。

• Teleforce的观点：Teleforce对MI350的规格参数表示赞赏，尤其是其配备的2304 GB HMB3E VRAM内存，突显了该硬件的高性能和适用性。

• Behnamoh的观点：Behnamoh关注MI350的市场供应问题，尤其是其是否像MI300一样仅以x8批次出售。这个问题影响了他的研究使用选择，最终选择了Nvidia的RTX Pro 6000。

• AbuAssar的观点：AbuAssar推测MI350使用CDNA架构（基于GCN），并猜测未来的MI400可能会跳过GCN直接转向RDNA 5。这涉及对AMD未来产品路线的预测和架构讨论。

• Tedunangst的观点：Tedunangst的评论比较轻松，提到某些提问质量，没有直接涉及技术讨论。

• Deadbabe的观点：Deadbabe提出了一个广泛的问题，即AMD是否能赶上Nvidia。这涉及对两家公司在市场竞争中的地位和未来发展的看法。

• Jonfromsf的观点：Jonfromsf认为Nvidia的优势不仅在于硬件，更在于软件生态。他指出，仅有更好的硬件不足以在市场竞争中取胜，强调了软件支持和市场竞争的综合因素。

补充讨论：
• 硬件性能与市场供应：Behnamoh和Latchkey对MI350的市场供应和实际使用体验提出看法，显示了即使硬件性能优越，供应策略也会影响用户选择。
• AMD与Nvidia的竞争：Deadbabe和Jonfromsf关注AMD与Nvidia的市场竞争，讨论了硬件之外的软件优势对竞争格局的影响。

争议焦点：
• AMD是否能赶上Nvidia：Deadbabe和Jonfromsf的评论中隐含了对AMD和Nvidia竞争结果的不同预期，争议点在于硬件之外的软件生态对竞争的影响。

Hello you fine Internet folks,
At AMD's Advancing AI 2025, I had the pleasure of interviewing Alan Smith, AMD Senior Fellow and Chief Instinct Architect, about CDNA4 found in the MI350 series of accelerators.
Hope y'all enjoy!
Transcript below has been edited for conciseness and readability.
George:
Hello you fine internet folks! We're here today at AMD's Advancing AI 2025 event, where the MI350 series has just been announced. And I have the pleasure to introduce, Alan Smith from AMD.
Alan:
Hello, everyone.
George:
What do you do at AMD?
Alan
: So I'm the chief architect of Instinct GPUs.
George
: Awesome, what does that job entail?
Alan
: So I'm responsible for the GPU product line definition, working with our data center GPU business partners to define the-, work with them on the definition of the requirements of the GPUs, and then work with the design teams to implement those requirements.
George:
Awesome. So, moving into MI350: MI350's still GFX9 based, and- for you guys in the audience, GFX9 is also known as Vega, or at least derivative of GFX9. Why is it that MI350 is still on GFX9, whereas clients such as RDNA 3 and 4, GFX11 and 12 respectively?
Alan:
Sure, yeah, it's a great question. So as you know, the CDNA architecture off of, you know, previous generations of Instinct GPUs, starting with MI100 and before, like you said, in the Vega generations, were all GCN architecture, which was Graphics Core Next. And over several generations, CDNA's been highly optimized for the types of distributed computing algorithms for high-performance computing and AI. And so we felt like starting with that base for MI350 would give us the right pieces that we needed to deliver the performance goals that we had for the MI350 series.
George:
And with GCN, as you know, there's a separate L1 cache and LDS, or Local Data Store. Why is that still in MI350? And why haven't they been merged?
Alan:
Yeah, so like you said, you know, it is a legacy piece of the GCN architecture. It's sort of fundamental to the way the compute unit is built. So we felt like in this generation, it wasn't the right opportunity to make a microarchitectural change of that scale. So what we did instead, was we increased the capacity of the LDS. So previously in MI300 series, we had a 64 kilobyte LDS, and we've increased that capacity to 160 kilobytes in MI350 series. And in addition to that, we increased the bandwidth as well. So we doubled the bandwidth of the LDS into the register file, in order to be able to feed the Tensor Core rates that we have in the MI350 series.
George:
And speaking of Tensor Cores, you've now introduced microscaling formats to MI350x for FP8, FP6, and FP4 data types. Interestingly enough, a major differentiator for MI350 is that FP6 is the same rate as FP4. Can you talk a little bit about how that was accomplished and why that is?
Alan:
Sure, yep, so one of the things that we felt like on MI350 in this timeframe, that it's going into the market and the current state of AI... we felt like that FP6 is a format that has potential to not only be used for inferencing, but potentially for training. And so we wanted to make sure that the capabilities for FP6 were class-leading relative to... what others maybe would have been implementing, or have implemented. And so, as you know, it's a long lead time to design hardware, so we were thinking about this years ago and wanted to make sure that MI350 had leadership in FP6 performance. So we made a decision to implement the FP6 data path at the same throughput as the FP4 data path. Of course, we had to take on a little bit more hardware in order to do that. FP6 has a few more bits, obviously, that's why it's called FP6. But we were able to do that within the area of constraints that we had in the matrix engine, and do that in a very power- and area-efficient way.
George:
And speaking of data types, I've noticed that TF32 is not on your ops list for hardware level acceleration. Why remove that feature from... or why was that not a major consideration for MI350?
Alan:
Yeah, well, it was a consideration, right? Because we did remove it. We felt like that in this timeframe, that brain float 16, or BF16, would be a format that would be leverageable for most models to replace TF32. And we can deliver a much higher throughput on BF16 than TF32, so we felt like it was the right trade off for this implementation.
George:
And if I was to use TF32, what would the speed be? Would it still be FP32, the speed of FP32?
Alan:
You have a choice. We offer some emulation, and I don't have all the details on the exact throughputs off the top of

data.title: No More Shading Languages: Compiling C++ to Vulkan Shaders [pdf]
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕着在不同编程语言和环境下进行着色器编程（shader programming）的可行性、必要性及其技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• Calavar认为将以CPU为中心的代码移植到GPU上可能会导致性能下降，因为CPU和GPU之间存在巨大的阻抗不匹配。他质疑将80%非性能敏感的代码移植到GPU的合理性，并表示对为何有很多人对用CPU中心语言写着色器感兴趣存在疑惑。
• danybittel回应了关于着色器程序限制的问题，指出通过Vulkan的"Buffer device address"功能，可以使用物理指针。该功能最初是一个扩展，但现在已成为Vulkan标准的一部分，并在大多数GPU上可用，不过仅适用于缓冲区，不适用于图像或本地数组。
• fuhsnn讨论了当前渲染器未使用任何子组内在函数的问题，并指出由于LLVM未提供结构化控制流，无法实现最大重聚。他建议在C语言家族中增加此类模型，并在GPU编译器中实现，应成为未来研究的重点，并提到ispc语言可能适合此需求。
• canyp认为标准化CUDA模型是重要的进步，并指出将着色器程序与主源代码分离的传统方式已经过时。
• makotech221提到Stride3d引擎允许在C#中编写着色器并编译为GLSL，提供了一种更接近CPU语言的着色器编写方式。
• raincole以讽刺的语气评论了C++作为巅峰语言设计的观点，暗示对C++的复杂性和受欢迎程度的看法。
• rgbforge对Slang语言的某些技术细节感兴趣，特别是函数指针仅适用于Cuda目标这一点。
• genidoi认为GLSL已经很好，强调着色器不仅是程序，更是艺术作品，并通过提供具体例子说明了着色器的艺术价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是将CPU代码移植到GPU的合理性和性能问题，特别是关于CPU和GPU之间阻抗不匹配的问题。
• 另一个讨论点是关于着色器编程语言和工具的演进，包括对现有语言如C++、C#以及新语言如ispc的适用性讨论。
• 技术细节上，涉及了Vulkan的"Buffer device address"功能、LLVM的控制流结构、CUDA模型的标准化以及Slang语言的特性。
• 艺术性与技术性之间的平衡也被提及，强调了着色器在艺术创作中的独特价值。

data.title: AbsenceBench: Language models can't tell what's missing
data.author: JnBrymn
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为AbsenceBench的基准测试，用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）识别缺失信息的能力。尽管LLM在识别意外信息方面表现出色，但在识别明显遗漏的信息时仍存在困难。AbsenceBench通过数值序列、诗歌和GitHub拉取请求三个领域，要求模型在给定原始和编辑上下文的情况下，识别文档中被故意删除的部分。实验显示，即使是最先进的模型，如Claude-3.7-Sonnet，在处理平均5K tokens的上下文时，F1得分也只有69.6%。分析表明，这是由于Transformer注意力机制难以关注文档中的“空白”，因为这些缺失不对应于任何可被注意的特定键。研究揭示了模型在某些任务上的超人表现与在识别缺失信息任务上的意外崩溃之间的紧密关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在识别信息缺失和处理省略方面的能力和局限性

不同观点：
• birdfood 通过实验发现，Claude 在识别旋转后的 Kanizsa 三角形图像时表现不佳，无法正确识别隐含的三角形，表明模型在处理旋转图像和不完全信息时存在局限。
• cs702 提到，即使是最新的模型在识别上下文中被移除的信息时表现也较差，并指出这是由于 Transformer 的注意力机制无法关注被移除的 tokens。
• yousif_123123 提出几个观点：1) 虽然注意力机制无法精确定位 gaps，但微调可能有助于提高模型在这类任务上的表现；2) 较短的输入或较少的省略更难解决，类似于人类在面对类似情况时的困难；3) 推理模型在这类任务上表现更好，但仍未达到100%的准确性，这表明可能存在其他尚未明确识别的智能方面。
• XenophileJKO 认为，无法检测未分类的省略是预料之中的，因为注意力机制无法处理未定义的 omission，需要通过比较完整的上下文来实现。
• OsrsNeedsf2P 对 benchmarking 表示兴奋，认为这是向正确方向迈出的一步。
• itsgrimetime 认为，LLM 结合 diff 工具可能会达到 100% 的准确性，但这不是问题的核心。
• kadonoishi 指出，检测 absence 是更高阶的神经任务，可能目前是生物独有的能力，LLM 在这方面存在不足。
• b0a04gl 强调，模型的架构假设输入是完整的，因此无法检测缺失信息，需要在训练目标和输入编码上进行调整。
• jonbaer 通过引用“中文房间”理论，暗示 LLM 只是按照规则处理输入，而不真正“理解”内容。
• yandie 实验发现，视觉模型（如 Claude + Gemini）在识别图像差异时表现较好，但在图像翻转时表现下降。
• pkoird 询问是否有资源记录 LLMs 在不同任务上的表现优劣。
• obscure-enigma 认为，LLMs 是损失压缩器，简化和泛化信息是其固有特性，因此在处理某些任务时存在局限。
• AlienRobot 指出，LLM 无法识别“缺失”，因为任何输入都会被处理并给出输出，模型假设所有输入都是有效的。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点在于 LLM 是否能够有效检测信息的缺失，以及是否可以通过调整模型架构或训练方法来改善这一点。
• 视觉模型在处理图像差异时的表现也被提及，实验显示模型在旋转图像后识别能力下降，表明模型在处理空间变换时存在局限。
• 有人对 benchmarking 表示支持，认为这是推动模型改进的重要步骤，同时也有人指出 LLM 本质上是损失压缩器，在某些任务上存在固有局限。

Title:
AbsenceBench: Language Models Can't Tell What's Missing
Authors:
Harvey Yiyun Fu
,
Aryan Shrivastava
,
Jared Moore
,
Peter West
,
Chenhao Tan
,
Ari Holtzman
View a PDF of the paper titled AbsenceBench: Language Models Can't Tell What's Missing, by Harvey Yiyun Fu and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly capable of processing long inputs and locating specific information within them, as evidenced by their performance on the Needle in a Haystack (NIAH) test. However, while models excel at recalling surprising information, they still struggle to identify clearly omitted information. We introduce AbsenceBench to assesses LLMs' capacity to detect missing information across three domains: numerical sequences, poetry, and GitHub pull requests. AbsenceBench asks models to identify which pieces of a document were deliberately removed, given access to both the original and edited contexts. Despite the apparent straightforwardness of these tasks, our experiments reveal that even state-of-the-art models like Claude-3.7-Sonnet achieve only 69.6% F1-score with a modest average context length of 5K tokens. Our analysis suggests this poor performance stems from a fundamental limitation: Transformer attention mechanisms cannot easily attend to "gaps" in documents since these absences don't correspond to any specific keys that can be attended to. Overall, our results and analysis provide a case study of the close proximity of tasks where models are already superhuman (NIAH) and tasks where models breakdown unexpectedly (AbsenceBench).

44332699.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为AbsenceBench的基准测试，用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）识别缺失信息的能力。尽管LLM在识别意外信息方面表现出色，但在识别明显遗漏的信息时仍存在困难。AbsenceBench通过数值序列、诗歌和GitHub拉取请求三个领域，要求模型在给定原始和编辑上下文的情况下，识别文档中被故意删除的部分。实验显示，即使是最先进的模型，如Claude-3.7-Sonnet，在处理平均5K tokens的上下文时，F1得分也只有69.6%。分析表明，这是由于Transformer注意力机制难以关注文档中的“空白”，因为这些缺失不对应于任何可被注意的特定键。研究揭示了模型在某些任务上的超人表现与在识别缺失信息任务上的意外崩溃之间的紧密关系。

data.title: Smartphones: Parts of Our Minds? Or Parasites?
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能手机是否是人类认知系统的扩展、共生体或寄生体

不同观点：
• **roenxi的观点**：
  1. 认为文章摘要像意见表达，缺乏哲学期刊应有的客观和严谨。
  2. 自然界是混乱的，人体的一些部分（如免疫系统、肠道菌群、皮肤螨虫）可能是曾经的寄生体，经过进化成为共生体。
  3. 人类天生容易被操纵，这是社会动物的特性，而不是系统出问题的标志。
  4. 人类最大的敌人往往是自己的认知系统，因此说智能手机是“寄生体”是有可能的。

• **teekert的观点**：
  1. 智能手机等设备确实改变了人类，比如增强记忆力和提高时间管理能力。
  2. 认为文章讨论的问题可以归结为定义的不同，没必要把问题复杂化。
  3. 总体上对文章持轻松态度，觉得讨论的议题不那么重要。

• **lolive的观点**：
  1. 通过技术（如Obsidian笔记应用）增强自我，认为这些技术工具是积极的，帮助团队更好地管理知识。
  2. 投票支持智能手机是“人工内容成为我们思想的一部分”而不是寄生体。

• **elliotec的观点**：
  1. 强调智能手机是“共生体，有时是寄生体”。
  2. 认为共生体这一面更贴切。

• **voidhorse的观点**：
  1. 坚定认为智能手机是寄生体，充斥着各种不相关的信息，像寄生虫一样吸取主人的生命力。
  2. 描述使用智能手机的体验如同发烧梦境，是寄生体的表现。

• **metalman的观点**：
  1. 智能手机的搜索功能和文件管理混乱，使用户陷入迷宫，技术限制了信息的自由交换。
  2. 整体体验是智能手机像寄生体，阻碍了信息的有效获取和使用。

补充讨论：
1. **争议的焦点**在于智能手机是人类认知系统的扩展还是寄生体。roenxi和teekert更倾向于认为这是定义问题，而voidhorse和metalman则坚决认为智能手机是寄生体。
2. **elliotec**提出智能手机既有共生也有寄生特性，提供了一个较为平衡的视角。
3. **具体例子**如lolive使用Obsidian成功管理知识，和metalman对智能手机搜索功能的挫败感，进一步丰富了讨论的维度。

总体来看，讨论围绕智能手机对人类认知系统的影响，是积极的扩展还是消极的寄生体，存在不同立场和体验。

data.title: Proba-3's first artificial solar eclipse
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 欧洲航天局的Proba-3任务展示了其首次拍摄的太阳外层大气——日冕图像。该任务由两颗卫星组成，借助机载定位技术像单一航天器一样飞行，成功在轨道上创造了首次“人工全日食”。两颗卫星相距150米，相对位置精确到毫米级，其中一个卫星遮挡太阳强光，使另一个卫星上的ASPIICS仪器捕捉日冕图像。此任务不仅展示了编队飞行技术的精确性，还提供了宝贵的科学数据，有助于理解太阳及其神秘的大气层。Proba-3还将研究太阳风、日冕物质抛射等现象，并通过其他仪器测量太阳总辐照度和地球辐射带中的电子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太空技术中精密对准的技术成就及其在其他领域中的应用

不同观点：
• [hifikuno] 对现代科技的进步表示惊叹，特别提到两块金属物体在太空中相距数十米的情况下，能够精确地对准到毫米级别。他认为解决这样的问题非常复杂，自己无从下手。

• [prats226] 提出疑问，为什么望远镜不采用类似的精确对准技术。这暗示了对太空技术与地面望远镜技术应用不一致的困惑或质疑。

补充讨论：
• [hifikuno] 的评论强调了对太空科技精密程度的赞赏，尤其是距离和精度的对比带来了强烈的印象。

• [prats226] 的提问指出了潜在的技术应用问题，即为什么在望远镜设计中不直接应用类似的精密对准技术。这可能暗示了对不同技术领域间技术转移或应用差异的关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在为何精密的太空对准技术未广泛应用于望远镜等地面观测设备上，可能涉及技术实现的难度、成本效益或实际需求等问题。

ESA
/
Enabling & Support
/
Space Engineering & Technology
/
Proba-3
Today, the European Space Agency’s Proba-3 mission unveils its first images of the Sun’s outer atmosphere – the solar corona. The mission’s two satellites, able to fly as a single spacecraft thanks to a suite of onboard positioning technologies, have succeeded in creating their first ‘artificial total solar eclipse’ in orbit. The resulting coronal images demonstrate the potential of formation flying technologies, while delivering invaluable scientific data that will improve our understanding of the Sun and its enigmatic atmosphere.
Proba-3 infographic: Formation flying to a fingernail's thickness
Two spacecraft flying as one
This March, Proba-3 achieved what no other mission has before – its two spacecraft, the Coronagraph and the Occulter,
flew 150 metres apart in perfect formation
for several hours without any control from the ground.
While aligned, the pair maintain their relative position down to a single millimetre – an extraordinary feat enabled by
a set of innovative navigation and positioning technologies
.
Demonstrating the degree of precision achieved, the two spacecraft use their formation flying time to create artificial total solar eclipses in orbit – they align with the Sun so that the 1.4 m large disc carried by the Occulter spacecraft covers the bright disc of the Sun for the Coronagraph spacecraft, casting a shadow of 8 cm across onto its optical instrument,
ASPIICS
.
Proba-3 Occulter eclipsing Sun for Coronagraph spacecraft
This instrument, short for Association of Spacecraft for Polarimetric and Imaging Investigation of the Corona of the Sun, was developed for ESA by an industrial consortium led by
Centre Spatial de Liège
, Belgium. When its 5 cm aperture is covered by the shadow, the instrument captures images of the solar corona uninterrupted by the Sun’s bright light.
Observing the corona is crucial for revealing
solar wind
, the continuous flow of matter from the Sun into outer space. It is also necessary for understanding the workings of
coronal mass ejections
(CMEs), explosions of particles sent out by the Sun almost every day, especially during high activity periods.
Such events can create stunning auroras in the night sky but also pose serious threats to modern technology. They can significantly disrupt communications, power transmission, and navigation systems on Earth, as they did in
May 2024
.
Solar corona viewed by Proba-3’s ASPIICS
The coronal images resulting from the first rounds of ASPIICS’s observations
offer a glimpse of the valuable data we can expect from this eclipse-making mission.
Dietmar Pilz, ESA Director of Technology, Engineering and Quality, comments: “Many of the technologies which allowed Proba-3 to perform precise formation flying have been developed through ESA’s General Support Technology Programme, as has the mission itself. It is exciting to see these stunning images validate our technologies in what is now the world’s first precision formation flying mission.”
Solar corona viewed by Proba-3’s ASPIICS
The mysterious halo
The Sun's fiery corona reaches temperatures above a million degrees Celsius, much hotter than the surface beneath it.
This counterintuitive temperature difference
has long been a topic in the scientific community.
Proba-3’s ASPIICS is tackling this mystery by studying the corona very close to the Sun’s surface. It can also see more detail, detecting fainter features than traditional coronagraphs thanks to a drastic reduction in how much ‘stray’ light reaches the detector.
Joe Zender, Proba-3 project scientist, adds: “Seeing the first data from ASPIICS is incredibly exciting. Together with the measurements made by another instrument on board, DARA, ASPIICS will contribute to unravelling long-lasting questions about our home star.”
The
Digital Absolute Radiometer
(DARA) will measure the total solar irradiance – exactly how much energy the Sun is putting out at any one time. A third scientific instrument on Proba-3, the
3D Energetic Electron Spectrometer
(3DEES), will detect electrons in Earth’s radiation belts, measuring their direction of origin and energy levels.
Proba-3’s artificial solar eclipse
How to create a solar eclipse
“I was absolutely thrilled to see the images, especially since we got them on the first try,” comments Andrei Zhukov, Principal Investigator for ASPIICS at the
Royal Observatory of Belgium

The images were processed by the ASPIICS Science Operations Centre (SOC) hosted by the Royal Observatory of Belgium. Here, a dedicated team of scientists and engineers creates operational commands for the coronagraph based on requests from the scientific community and shares the resulting observations.

data.author: Zealotux
data.article_summary: 一项由ANSES进行的研究旨在检测饮料中的微塑料污染水平，重点分析容器类型对污染水平的影响。结果出乎意料，玻璃瓶装饮料（如可乐、柠檬水、冰茶和啤酒）中的微塑料含量高于其他容器，平均每升含有约100个微塑料颗粒，而塑料瓶和罐中的含量则低五到五十倍。对于水，无论容器类型，微塑料水平都较低。研究发现，玻璃瓶装饮料中的微塑料可能来源于瓶盖上的油漆。通过清洁瓶盖，可以显著减少微塑料含量，例如吹气处理后含量从287个颗粒/升降至106个颗粒/升，再经过冲洗后降至87个颗粒/升。为减少微塑料污染，建议制造商改进瓶盖存储条件和油漆成分。

The aim of the ANSES study was to determine the level of microplastic contamination in drinks such as water, soda, iced tea, wine and beer; it also sought to establish the impact of their containers on this level. For most of the drinks studied,
the level of microplastics was found to be higher in glass bottles
than in other containers. For example, on average, in glass bottles of cola, lemonade, iced tea and beer, there were around 100 microplastic particles per litre. This number was five to 50 times lower in plastic bottles and cans.
“
We were expecting the opposite result when we compared the level of microplastics in different drinks sold in France
” explains Iseline Chaïb, a PhD student in the Aquatic Food Safety Unit (SANAQUA, Boulogne-sur-Mer site), which conducted the study at the ANSES Laboratory for Food Safety. In the absence of toxicological reference data, it is not possible to say whether the levels of microplastics found pose a health risk. The thesis was co-funded by the Hauts-de-France Region and ANSES. The project also received support under the IDEAL State-Region plan contract and from the French National Research Agency (IFSEA University Research School).
In the specific case of water
, the level of
microplastics was relatively low regardless of the container
, with an average of 4.5 particles per litre in glass bottles and 1.6 particles per litre in plastic bottles and cartons. Wine also contained few microplastics, including in glass bottles with corks. The origin of these variations in the level of microplastics in drinks remains to be explored, except for drinks contained in glass bottles with caps.
Plastic particles in drinks come from the paint on the caps
The scientists investigated the origin of the microplastics found in drinks packaged in glass bottles with caps. Given their characteristics, they concluded that these particles probably came from the
metal caps, and more specifically from the paint that covered them
. The first clue: the microplastics found in the drinks were mostly the same colour and had the same composition as the paint on the caps. The second clue: the paint on these caps had tiny scratches that were invisible to the naked eye and had probably been caused by friction between the caps when they were stored before use. This friction, which released particles from the surface of the caps, was thought to be the source of the microplastics found.
Clean caps before sealing bottles to reduce the level of microplastics
To confirm the route of contamination of drinks in glass bottles and explore the possibility of reducing microplastic levels,
the laboratory tested the effects of different cleaning operations
. “
We studied three scenarios” explains the PhD student. “We cleaned the bottles and filled them with filtered water so that no microplastics could be detected, then we placed caps on the bottles without treating the caps, after blowing on the caps with an air bomb, or after blowing air and rinsing the caps with filtered water and alcohol
”.
The result? While an average of 287 particles per litre were found in the water of the bottles sealed with uncleaned caps, this number decreased significantly, to 106 particles per litre, when air was blown on the caps before they were placed on the bottles. It fell further to 87 particles per litre when blowing was followed by rinsing.
To prevent plastic particles from being released into drinks contained in bottles sealed with caps, manufacturers could also explore other lines of action, such as changing the conditions in which the caps are stored before use, to avoid friction, or modifying the composition of the paint used on the caps.

Read the publication “Microplastic contaminations in a set of beverages sold in France

data.title: AtomicOS – A security-first OS with real crypto and deterministic language
data.author: ipenas-cl
data.article_summary: AtomicOS是一个从零构建、以安全为核心的教育性操作系统。它实现了真实的安全特性，包括AES-128加密、SHA-256哈希、内存管理单元（MMU）、内存保护和栈保护等。系统采用自定义的引导程序，支持保护模式和两级分页，并集成了Tempo编程语言，该语言支持确定性执行和最坏情况执行时间（WCET）分析。项目包含多个版本，其中v0.4实现了MMU，v0.3侧重安全设计，并提供了简单的视觉演示。开发环境需要i686-elf-gcc、nasm和qemu-system-i386等工具。项目文件结构包括内核、Tempo语言编译器和文档等部分。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个代码项目（可能涉及安全性）的可行性和实现细节的质疑

不同观点：
• [kragen] 对项目中的技术细节表示质疑，特别是如何在复杂的硬件环境下（如TLB misses、System Management Mode、缓存未命中等）确保代码能在100纳秒内完成执行。他提出了具体的技术难题，并对项目声称的性能表示怀疑。

• [jiveturkey] 认为该项目更像是一个玩笑，理由包括：
  - 项目使用了C语言，而不是在2025年被认为新颖的技术，这与它声称的"security-first"标签不符。
  - 项目版本为v0.5，但没有包含任何授权（authz）原语，与其安全性的宣称不匹配。
  - 对项目描述中夸张的宣传语（如“Military Grade - Navy SEAL Level Security”）表示嘲讽，认为其实际内容与宣传不符。

补充讨论：
• [jiveturkey] 提到虽然对项目的浮夸描述有反感，但对项目中的"tempo"部分有一定好感，表明对项目某些方面的设计或创意可能持开放态度。

争议焦点：
• 该项目是否能够如宣传所言，提供高安全性及高性能。
• 使用C语言开发是否合适，尤其是在安全性和新颖性方面。
• 项目是否真正具备其所宣称的安全特性，特别是缺乏授权原语的问题。
• 对项目描述中夸张的语言和实际技术能力之间的差距存在质疑。

AtomicOS
A security-first operating system built from scratch with real memory protection, cryptography, and a deterministic programming language.
🎯 Overview
AtomicOS is an educational operating system that prioritizes security over performance. Unlike many hobby OS projects, it implements real security features including AES-128 encryption, SHA-256 hashing, and a complete Memory Management Unit (MMU).
Philosophy
: "Seguridad primero, luego estabilidad y luego performance" (Security first, then stability, then performance)
✨ Features
Core Kernel (v0.4)
✅ Custom bootloader (Multiboot compliant)
✅ Protected mode with stack protection
✅ Memory Management Unit (MMU) with 2-level paging
✅ Physical and virtual memory management
✅ VGA text mode with color support
Security Features
✅
Real AES-128 encryption
(not XOR!)
✅
SHA-256 cryptographic hashing
✅ Memory guards and bounds checking
✅ W^X (Write XOR Execute) enforcement
✅ Secure memory wiping on free
✅ Page-level access control
Tempo Programming Language
✅ Deterministic execution
✅ Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET) analysis
✅ Compiles to x86 assembly
✅ Integrated runtime in kernel
🚀 Quick Start
Prerequisites
i686-elf-gcc
(cross-compiler for x86)
nasm
(Netwide Assembler)
qemu-system-i386
(for testing)
make
Building
#
Build AtomicOS v0.4 with MMU
make -f Makefile.v4
#
Run in QEMU
./run_mmu.sh
Other Versions
#
v0.3 - Security-first design
make -f Makefile.v3
./run_atomicos.sh
#
Simple visual demo
make -f Makefile.demo
./ver_demo.sh
